Holmes has shown you enough to make the coming vigil a sober thing: the cigar smell through the ventilator, the bed clamped beneath the dummy bell-rope, the chair, the milk, the lash. Your revolver is in your pocket, and the next step will not be taken until you choose the manner of your own resolve.
branching_choices.choice_question: How do you commit yourself to the night's vigil with Holmes?

options.label: A
options.text: You tell Holmes that whatever waits in that room, you will go with him because Helen must not face one more night of that contrivance alone.
options.outcome: You answer at once, and from the heart rather than from the tactical mind. Whatever the hidden agency may prove to be, you say, one thing is already clear: a woman has slept too long under an arrangement made for her destruction, and if there is one more night to be endured, she shall not endure it undefended. Holmes gives you a look which in another man might have been called warm. He says little, but there is approval in the brevity with which he turns from your declaration to the practical details of entry. The darkness beyond the inn-window seems no less black for your resolve, yet it becomes a darkness entered for someone, not merely against something. Then, across the grounds, a light springs up in the middle window.
options.downstream_effect: Your commitment frames the vigil as a protective stand, strengthening moral resolve and Helen-centred focus going into Session 2.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Watson's revolver remains carried and ready

options.world_noticed_signal: Holmes ceases to test your nerve and begins to use it. The room at Stoke Moran, still distant, seems already to have drawn a line from its window to your hand upon the pistol.
options.defining_line: You go because someone must stand between terror and the bed.
options.next_session_opens: The middle window burns like a small summons in the dark, and you cross the lawn with the loaded pistol heavy in your coat.

options.label: B
options.text: You say that you will go, but only after the signal is tested in your mind once more, for courage without precaution would merely serve Roylott's purpose.
options.outcome: You do not draw back, but neither will you flatter danger by mistaking haste for bravery. Before the move is made, you ask Holmes to walk once more through the order of things: Helen's lamp, her withdrawal, your approach by the lawn, the silent entry, the waiting in darkness. He complies without impatience, setting each step in its place with that admirable exactness which is itself a kind of courage. The repetition steadies the imagination by giving it rails. When you finally declare yourself ready, it is not with flourish but with composed assent. Holmes answers, "Very good," and the phrase carries more fellowship than praise. At that instant the expected light appears, sharp and steady, in the middle window across the grounds.
options.downstream_effect: The vigil begins from a posture of disciplined caution, improving procedural readiness and tightening Holmes's operational trust.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Watson's revolver remains carried and ready

options.world_noticed_signal: The plan, once repeated, seems to settle into the room like furniture placed for use. Even the coming darkness appears less shapeless when each movement has been named.
options.defining_line: You mistrust brave confusion more than you fear the night.
options.next_session_opens: The signal shines with unnerving steadiness, and you move only after every step of the dreadful vigil has been set in order.

options.label: C
options.text: You propose that before going straight to the window you first take one circuit of the grounds, to learn whether Roylott or one of his beasts is already abroad.
options.outcome: Your readiness takes the form not of retreat but of one last irregular precaution. Before trusting the direct path, you propose a short circuit of the grounds, for Roylott is no ordinary adversary and the cheetah and baboon are facts, not fancies. Holmes considers, then inclines his head, seeing that the suggestion springs from danger honestly reckoned rather than from shrinking. The plan is thereby made a shade more hazardous in time, yet perhaps less blind in execution. You rise together and stand for a moment at the inn-window, measuring hedge, lawn, and dark mass of house as though the very grounds might answer. Then the lamp appears at last, and what was conjecture becomes summons.
options.downstream_effect: The next session will open with a more wary, grounds-aware approach, increasing tension around noise, animals, and Roylott's possible alertness.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Watson's revolver remains carried and ready

options.world_noticed_signal: The lawn ceases to be mere distance and becomes contested ground. House, hedge, and dark outbuildings take on the look of positions in a field operation.
options.defining_line: You would rather meet danger sideways than walk into its mouth blind.
options.next_session_opens: With the lamp newly kindled, you leave the inn not for the window at once, but for a listening circuit beneath the wandering beasts and the black trees.

branching_choices.all_paths_arrive_at: Session end. The signal appears, the vigil is imminent, and Session 2 opens on the execution of the chosen commitment posture.

canon_boundaries: Watson must commit to accompany Holmes into the night operation; he cannot abandon the vigil.
The vigil itself, the whistle, the strike, and Roylott's death are reserved for Session 2.
The signal lamp appears and launches the operation in all paths.

character_truth.authentic_reaction_to_unexpected_input: Holmes accepts courage best when it is serviceable. He approves loyalty, respects disciplined review, and may adopt a prudent irregularity if it does not betray nerve.
Helen is offstage, but the manner of your commitment affects how the coming operation is narrated and how ready you are to answer her signal.

scene_integrity.character_knowledge_limits: You know the clue-chain strongly enough to suspect a subtle and horrible crime, but you have not yet seen the living method at work.
scene_integrity.emotional_context: Nightfall, compressed dread, and the difference between agreeing to danger in theory and stepping toward it in fact.

fold_back_path.nearest_safe_outcome: You accompany Holmes toward the vigil with a defined risk posture that colours the opening of Session 2.
fold_back_path.why: The retention hook depends on the player's unresolved decision about how to enter the dreadful vigil, not whether to enter it at all.

freeform_alignment_mapping.maps_to_chaotic: Adding an irregular precaution, scouting, or other boundary-breaking adjustment before the planned entry.
freeform_alignment_mapping.maps_to_lawful: Insisting on step-by-step review, readiness, and procedural caution before moving.
freeform_alignment_mapping.maps_to_neutral: Committing on humane protective grounds, placing Helen's safety above tactical self-display or theoretical completeness.
freeform_alignment_mapping.spirit_at_this_moment: The choice ends the session on your own chosen shape of courage, warm, disciplined, or wary.

branching_choices.cross_session_payoff_reference: Branch opportunity: courage_vs_caution. Payoff in Session 2 through Watson's steadiness, descriptive options, and readiness during the vigil.

emotional_choices.source_moment: Helen lowers her veil and says, "It is fear, Mr. Holmes. It is terror."
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: The words are simple, but the face behind them is more eloquent than any speech. Fear has done its work upon her before ever she reaches Baker Street.
emotional_choices.choice_question: How do you receive her terror in that first exposed instant?

options.label: A
options.text: You tell her quietly that she is among friends and may speak without fear.
options.outcome: You speak very little, which is perhaps why the words carry. The assurance is not theatrical, nor does it trespass upon Holmes's office; it merely gives the frightened lady one more human foothold in the room. She inclines her head with a gratitude too weary for flourish, and when she resumes, her sentences come more continuously, as though some inner check had eased. Holmes lets the comfort stand and proceeds at once to business, which is his own form of mercy. The room becomes less a place of exposure than a place of account.
options.tonal_effect: Narration warms slightly, with more humane shading around Helen's testimony.
options.world_noticed_signal: Helen's gloved fingers loosen upon one another. The firelight reaches her face, and she no longer keeps wholly to the window's edge.

options.label: B
options.text: You incline your head and leave the silence clear for Holmes's questions.
options.outcome: You judge that the kindest service may be not to crowd the moment with a second reassurance. Holmes has already taken the lead, and the lady has come for ordered help. By holding your peace and giving her your full attention, you lend the interview the gravity of a consultation rather than the confusion of competing sympathies. She notices the restraint, and though it does not comfort her, neither does it unsettle her. Her account begins under the sign of seriousness, with every tremor made the more audible by the quiet around it.
options.tonal_effect: Narration grows cooler and more procedural, emphasizing witness form and precise attention.
options.world_noticed_signal: No one interrupts the silence after her confession, and for that reason it deepens. Holmes's next question falls into it like an instrument laid upon a table.

options.label: C
options.text: You ask whether she has been followed or physically harmed before she says more.
options.outcome: The question comes sharply, perhaps more sharply than gentleness would have chosen, yet it has the merit of immediate relevance. Helen starts, then answers in fragments, enough to show that her fear is not mere nervous fancy but tied to a household where violence is possible. Holmes glances at you, quick and measuring, then takes up the line with greater precision. The effect upon the room is to turn terror at once toward danger of a practical kind. Comfort is deferred, but urgency gains contour, and Helen herself seems to understand that you are listening not for melodrama, but for threat.
options.tonal_effect: Narration tightens, shifting from pity toward hazard assessment.
options.world_noticed_signal: The interview acquires an edge at once. Fear is no longer an atmosphere only, but the possible preface to injury.

emotional_choices.all_paths_arrive_at: Holmes demonstrates the return-ticket and mud-splashes deduction, and Helen begins her fuller account.

emotional_choices.source_moment: After Julia's death account, Holmes probes the whistle, metallic clang, and sealed-room facts.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: The dreadful cry of "the speckled band" still seems to hang in the room, yet Holmes at once begins separating sound from impression, fact from horror. You may follow him there, or resist the chill of it.
emotional_choices.choice_question: What do you fix upon in the aftermath of Helen's account?

options.label: A
options.text: You press gently for the exact order of whistle, clang, unlocked door, and match.
options.outcome: You take the account as a coroner might, but with more courtesy than a coroner often shows. Sequence, in such matters, is half the truth. Helen, seeing that you seek not to doubt her but to preserve the shape of the event, answers with painful care: the whistle first, then the clanging sound, then the slow opening of the door, then Julia in the corridor with the charred match and box. The horror remains, but it is now pinned to order. Holmes's questions thereafter proceed more swiftly, as though you had cleared a path through undergrowth.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes more exact and evidentiary, with emphasis on sequence and object.
options.world_noticed_signal: Helen's recollection, though painful, settles into numbered particulars. The case begins to resist confusion.

options.label: B
options.text: You dwell on the dying words and ask what Helen herself believed them to mean.
options.outcome: There are moments when a witness's own sense of an event, however uncertain, is itself a fact. You therefore return not first to hinges and bars, but to Julia's last desperate phrase and to Helen's own attempts to live beside it for two years. Her answer is hesitant, self-correcting, and all the more valuable for that. She speaks of gipsies, spotted handkerchiefs, delirium, and ignorance, and in that uncertainty the case reveals something of its true cruelty. Holmes hears her out without impatience, though his fingers remain steepled and still.
options.tonal_effect: Narration balances human bewilderment with clue-minded attention.
options.world_noticed_signal: The phrase "speckled band" seems to linger the longer for being admitted as a wound, not yet an answer.

options.label: C
options.text: You ask at once whether any ordinary poison or human intruder was ever truly possible.
options.outcome: You leap over the lament to the impossibility, and though the movement is abrupt, it is not foolish. If the room was sealed, if no marks of violence were found, if poison left no trace, then every ordinary avenue narrows at once. Helen answers as best she can, and Holmes takes the question up with visible interest, sounding walls and barred shutters already in his mind. The effect is to harden the mystery rapidly. One feels less the sorrow of a death now past than the active pressure of a mechanism not yet understood.
options.tonal_effect: Narration sharpens into locked-room pressure and intellectual unease.
options.world_noticed_signal: Doors, bars, chimney staples, and match-stump rise in the mind like items laid out for inspection. The room at Stoke Moran begins to exist before you have seen it.

emotional_choices.all_paths_arrive_at: The sealed-room facts are established, and the case deepens toward immediate peril for Helen.

emotional_choices.source_moment: Holmes exposes the bruises on Helen's wrist after she reveals she now sleeps in Julia's room and heard again the whistle.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: The marks are small, but they alter the whole moral temperature of the interview. What had been terror becomes abuse made visible.
emotional_choices.choice_question: How do you answer the sight of the bruised wrist?

options.label: A
options.text: You speak with open anger at the man who could leave such marks upon her.
options.outcome: The words break from you before caution has quite had its say. They are not ungentle toward Helen, but they are hot with the instant verdict any decent man must feel. For a moment she looks less ashamed than relieved, as though the visible fact had at last released her from the burden of minimizing it. Holmes does not echo the indignation, yet neither does he check it; he merely turns the emotional truth into practical urgency. The case is no longer a strange old story. It is a present violence in need of interruption.
options.tonal_effect: Narration grows sterner and more morally charged.
options.world_noticed_signal: Helen's sleeve falls back over the wrist, but the room does not recover its earlier neutrality. The marks remain present even when hidden.

options.label: B
options.text: You tell Helen with grave gentleness that the marks are proof enough that she was right to come.
options.outcome: You do not inflame the moment, but neither do you let it pass as a mere exhibit. Instead you return the fact to Helen herself, not as shame, but as vindication. She has not imagined danger, nor exaggerated it; her body carries its own evidence. The effect upon her is immediate and touching. She straightens a little, and though fear remains, there enters into it the first faint element of being believed. Holmes, who values useful truth over emotional display, profits by the steadier witness that follows.
options.tonal_effect: Narration softens around Helen while preserving urgency.
options.world_noticed_signal: For the first time since her arrival, Helen seems less like a hunted creature than a woman to whom justice may yet be done.

options.label: C
options.text: You say nothing and let the bruises stand as evidence while Holmes turns at once to action.
options.outcome: Silence, here, is not indifference but discipline. The marks require no rhetoric, and to embroider them might only increase Helen's distress. You therefore let the evidence stand in its own dreadful plainness while Holmes converts it into decision. The result is severe, perhaps, but effective. The interview pivots from witness to operation with almost medical rapidity. Helen may draw less comfort from the restraint, yet she is spared a scene, and the business of getting to Stoke Moran that day advances without waste.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes clipped and operational, minimizing commentary.
options.world_noticed_signal: No one disputes what the wrist declares. The room seems to shorten the distance between Baker Street and Stoke Moran.

emotional_choices.all_paths_arrive_at: Helen departs, the same-day trip is resolved upon, and Roylott's interruption follows.

emotional_choices.source_moment: Roylott bursts into Baker Street, threatens Holmes, bends the poker, and departs; Holmes later straightens it.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: The man fills the doorway as though violence itself had put on a frock-coat. Holmes meets him with weather-talk and civility, which leaves you to decide what sort of witness you will be under threat.
emotional_choices.choice_question: How do you carry yourself through Roylott's display?

options.label: A
options.text: You hold yourself still and let Holmes's composure govern the room.
options.outcome: You feel the instinct to rise, yet master it, seeing that Holmes has already chosen the better weapon. Roylott's rage spends itself against courtesy, and your stillness denies him the secondary triumph of having disordered the whole room. When he bends the poker and flings down his threat, the act lands as brutality rather than dominance. Holmes's later straightening of the steel becomes, for you, not a mere feat of strength, but the proper answer of control to violence. The scene passes without your adding fuel to it.
options.tonal_effect: Narration remains cool and gentlemanly, emphasizing measured nerve.
options.world_noticed_signal: Roylott finds no second adversary to bait. The room, though invaded, is not surrendered.

options.label: B
options.text: You rise half from your chair, ready to interpose if Roylott advances another step.
options.outcome: The movement is instinctive and honest. You do not speak over Holmes, but your body has already declared that the man shall not lay hands where he pleases. Roylott notices, and for an instant his small eyes flick toward you with the ugly measuring look of a bully choosing his next object. Holmes's calm words then reclaim the scene before it can tip further. Afterwards, when the poker is straightened, your own readiness seems less a mistake than a reminder that civility in such rooms rests upon the possibility of force behind it.
options.tonal_effect: Narration tightens and shortens, with stronger bodily emphasis.
options.world_noticed_signal: A chair-leg sounds softly upon the floorboards, and Roylott's gaze catches it at once. Men like him are quick to read resistance in muscle before they hear it in words.

options.label: C
options.text: You watch him closely, fixing his features, dress, crop, and hands in memory for later judgment.
options.outcome: Rather than answer menace with counter-menace, you commit the man to memory. The top-hat, the gaiters, the hunting-crop, the great yellow face, the seared skin, the bird-of-prey nose, the knotted hands upon the poker, all are entered in that inward ledger by which one later understands a case more justly. Roylott leaves behind not only fear but data. Thus, when Holmes lightly remarks upon the decided draught and later bends the steel back again, the contrast acquires its full force. One man has displayed power; the other has measured it and remained master of himself.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes observational and classificatory, storing menace as evidence.
options.world_noticed_signal: The details of Roylott's person seem to remain in the room after he has gone, as tangible in recollection as the bent steel upon the hearth.

emotional_choices.all_paths_arrive_at: Holmes straightens the poker, returns with motive clarity, and prepares the departure for Surrey.

emotional_choices.source_moment: In the middle bedroom, the dummy bell-rope and the ventilator which does not ventilate are discovered.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: At last the house ceases to be merely oppressive and becomes intelligible in parts. Wrongness has taken physical form, and there is a singular pleasure in that, even under dread.
emotional_choices.choice_question: How do you answer this first true pattern of clues?

options.label: A
options.text: You confess your astonishment that ordinary household objects could be made so false.
options.outcome: The admission is no disgrace, for astonishment is the just tribute paid by honest minds to a subtle arrangement. A bell-rope that rings nothing, a ventilator opening where no air is wanted, a bed fixed where no bed need be fixed, the room has begun to declare itself in a language at once homely and monstrous. Holmes, hearing your wonder, allows himself the faintest answering gleam. It is one of his pleasures to see reason take hold where superstition might once have bred. For a brief interval the case yields not terror only, but intellectual delight.
options.tonal_effect: Narration brightens with Holmesian clue-pleasure while retaining menace.
options.world_noticed_signal: Even the dusty room seems altered once its innocence is broken. Common things no longer consent to be common.

options.label: B
options.text: You begin at once to connect rope, ventilator, and bed as parts of one deliberate arrangement.
options.outcome: Wonder gives place in you almost immediately to relation. A clue alone is odd; three clues in mechanical correspondence are design. You trace with your eye the line from opening to rope, from rope to pillow, from pillow to the fixed bed, and though the final agency escapes you still, the room has ceased to be a miscellany of eccentricities. Holmes notices the movement of your thought and answers it with one of those brief approvals more valuable than praise. The discovery becomes not merely striking, but usable.
options.tonal_effect: Narration turns analytic and structural, emphasizing clue linkage.
options.world_noticed_signal: The room seems to draw its lines tighter under your gaze. Each object points, and all point the same way.

options.label: C
options.text: You recoil a little from the room's wrongness and ask what sort of mind could devise it.
options.outcome: The response is less to mechanism than to moral imagination. One may catalogue the rope, the hook, the opening, and the clamped bed, yet there remains the colder question of what human patience and ingenuity turned these domestic fixtures into a trap. Holmes does not answer fully, but his face darkens in that singular way it has when intellect and wickedness are found in alliance. The room becomes, through your question, not only an evidentiary chamber but a moral one. The pleasure of discovery is touched at once with loathing.
options.tonal_effect: Narration deepens from clue-pleasure into moral dread.
options.world_noticed_signal: The dummy bell-rope hangs with a more sinister stillness once its purpose is suspected. The room feels less old than intentional.

emotional_choices.all_paths_arrive_at: The inquiry moves into Roylott's chamber, where the safe, saucer, chair, and lash complete the sinister inventory.

posture_shifts.placement: early Setup, before you fully answer Holmes at the bedside.
posture_shifts.narrator_line: The improper hour, the thin light, and Holmes already dressed make the room feel less like a bedroom than the first page of a case.

options.label: A
options.text: You glance first at the mantel clock.
options.stance_revealed: You orient by fact before feeling.
options.narration_adjustment: The hands stand at a quarter-past seven, an hour at which Holmes is seldom astir. The very impropriety of it gives the summons weight.

options.label: B
options.text: You study Holmes's face before speaking.
options.stance_revealed: You read danger through people first.
options.narration_adjustment: There is no flurry in him, only that quiet alertness which means business of an uncommon sort. The look steadies your own surprise into readiness.

options.label: C
options.text: You swing your feet down at once.
options.stance_revealed: You answer pressure with immediate motion.
options.narration_adjustment: Resentment has hardly time to form before habit and loyalty overtake it. The case has you before the explanation does.

posture_shifts.placement: late Setup, as Helen unveils and the fire is offered.
posture_shifts.narrator_line: When the veil lifts, the room asks whether you mean to receive a witness, a patient, or a frightened lady who is somehow all three.

options.label: A
options.text: You draw a chair a little nearer the fire.
options.stance_revealed: You soften rooms before you question people.
options.narration_adjustment: The small courtesy costs nothing and alters the interview at once. Helen's gratitude is visible before it is spoken.

options.label: B
options.text: You remain where you are and listen.
options.stance_revealed: You prefer not to disturb the formal shape of inquiry.
options.narration_adjustment: Distance preserves order. The room settles around Holmes's questions with the severity of a consultation.

options.label: C
options.text: You note the glove, veil, and hair in silence.
options.stance_revealed: You translate distress into observable particulars.
options.narration_adjustment: Premature grey, hunted eyes, black dress, return ticket half-hidden in the glove, each item enters the case at once. Pity does not exclude observation.

posture_shifts.placement: mid Escalation, inside Helen's compressed family-history testimony.
posture_shifts.narrator_line: Her account stretches backward through ruined family, Indian years, and village terror, and you must decide what sort of thread to keep hold of.

options.label: A
options.text: You follow the money in the story.
options.narration_adjustment: The bequest, the daughters' marriages, the shrinking income, these begin to separate themselves from the mass of household wretchedness. What looked like mere history starts to look like pressure.

options.label: B
options.text: You keep your ear on Roylott's violence.
options.narration_adjustment: The blacksmith in the stream, the prison term, the village fleeing at his approach, these facts gather around the man's name like storm-signs. The household becomes dangerous before it becomes mysterious.

options.label: C
options.text: You attend to the animals and gipsies.
options.stance_revealed: You lean toward the ominous and irregular.
options.narration_adjustment: Cheetah, baboon, wandering camps, spotted kerchiefs, all the loose and lawless edges of the estate press forward. The case acquires misdirection even before you can prove it such.

posture_shifts.placement: during Julia account, while Helen relives the fatal night.
posture_shifts.narrator_line: Her memory comes in a long unbroken current, and interruption itself becomes a moral choice.

options.label: A
options.text: You let her finish before you question.
options.narration_adjustment: The dreadful narrative runs its course without being broken upon the rack of inquiry. When the questions come, they come after the grief has earned its full shape.

options.label: B
options.text: You interject at the whistle.
options.stance_revealed: You seize on anomalies the instant they surface.
options.narration_adjustment: The low clear sound catches you as it caught Julia. The account briefly narrows around that one recurring note in the night.

options.label: C
options.text: You wait for the dying words.
options.stance_revealed: You listen for the case's central wound.
options.narration_adjustment: Everything in the story seems to move toward the corridor-lamp and the final cry. When it comes, the phrase lands with the force of a clue and a lament together.

posture_shifts.placement: late testimony-close, at the instant the wrist bruises are exposed.
posture_shifts.narrator_line: The five livid marks do more than prove violence, they ask what kind of anger you permit yourself.

options.label: A
options.text: Your jaw sets before you speak.
options.stance_revealed: You contain indignation rather than perform it.
options.narration_adjustment: The anger is there, but harnessed. It goes to strengthen decision rather than scatter itself in words.

options.label: B
options.text: You look first to Helen's face, not the marks.
options.stance_revealed: You centre the person over the evidence.
options.narration_adjustment: Shame, fear, and relief pass over her more quickly than the eye can catalogue. The bruises matter, but so does the burden of being seen to bear them.

options.label: C
options.text: You fix the pattern of thumb and fingers.
options.stance_revealed: You turn outrage into forensic certainty.
options.narration_adjustment: The white wrist with its printed violence enters the case as clean proof. Whatever vagueness haunted the earlier fears is lessened by this one plain exhibit.

posture_shifts.placement: during Roylott confrontation, while he looms in the doorway with hunting-crop and threat.
posture_shifts.narrator_line: A bully of that magnitude changes the air in a room, and the body decides some things before the tongue does.

options.label: A
options.text: You shift your weight forward, ready if needed.
options.stance_revealed: You meet threat with embodied readiness.
options.narration_adjustment: The movement is slight, but not invisible. Roylott sees enough to know that Holmes is not alone.

options.label: B
options.text: You keep one hand on the chair-arm.
options.narration_adjustment: Readiness remains private, which is often the safer form of courage. Holmes's composure has room to work because you do not crowd it.

options.label: C
options.text: You do not move at all.
options.narration_adjustment: Immobility can be its own answer to intimidation. Roylott spends his violence upon the room and receives no visible disorder in return.

posture_shifts.placement: post-confrontation, as Holmes straightens the poker.
posture_shifts.narrator_line: The steel answers his hands with a slow obedience, and the moment permits either relief or a darker reading.

options.label: A
options.text: You allow yourself a dry breath of relief.
options.stance_revealed: You use humour to release pressure.
options.narration_adjustment: The answer to brute force has been made without noise. For a moment the case admits the faintest Holmesian lightness.

options.label: B
options.text: You study the straightened steel in silence.
options.stance_revealed: You let symbols work upon you quietly.
options.narration_adjustment: The poker lies plain again, but not innocent. One remembers both the strength that bent it and the cooler strength that answered.

options.label: C
options.text: You ask whether Helen was followed here.
options.stance_revealed: You turn immediately from display to consequence.
options.narration_adjustment: The question cuts through spectacle to peril. If Roylott traced her to Baker Street, the case has already entered a more dangerous stage.

posture_shifts.placement: arrival at Stoke Moran, under the architect cover story.
posture_shifts.narrator_line: The grey gables stand before you, and even the harmless lie about architecture has its own moral flavour.

options.label: A
options.text: You wear the cover story easily.
options.stance_revealed: You accept discretion as part of protection.
options.narration_adjustment: The fiction sits neatly enough upon the visit to pass without strain. Such courtesies to danger are often wiser than declarations.

options.label: B
options.text: You dislike the pretence, but keep it.
options.stance_revealed: You obey tactical necessity without loving it.
options.narration_adjustment: The concealment leaves a slight taste of constraint, yet you do not spoil it by clumsy honesty. The work must be done before truth can be spoken aloud.

options.label: C
options.text: You let Holmes do the talking here.
options.stance_revealed: You know when another man is the better instrument.
options.narration_adjustment: Holmes carries the harmless professional air with practised ease. Your own silence helps the lie by not overworking it.

posture_shifts.placement: during Breath beat, at the discovery of the dummy bell-rope and inward ventilator.
posture_shifts.narrator_line: The room has at last begun to confess, and your attention may lean toward delight, revulsion, or pattern.

options.label: A
options.text: You bend nearer to the rope and hook.
options.stance_revealed: You are drawn toward the mechanism itself.
options.narration_adjustment: The thick cord, the idle tassel, the hook above, each repays nearness. Wrongness becomes most persuasive when touched by the eye at close range.

options.label: B
options.text: You look from ventilator to pillow.
options.stance_revealed: You instinctively map danger onto the body.
options.narration_adjustment: The line between opening and sleeper is too direct to be innocent. The bed's position begins to feel less accidental with every glance.

options.label: C
options.text: You step back to see the whole arrangement.
options.narration_adjustment: Seen together, the room's objects cease to be furniture and become apparatus. The old chamber acquires the chill of deliberate construction.

scene_rules_layer_4.character_knowledge_limits: Only Holmes knows a young lady in excitement waits below. Watson knows nothing yet of Helen's name, Roylott, Julia, Stoke Moran, or the whistle.
scene_rules_layer_4.emotional_context: Improper hour, intimate interruption, unease sharpened by Holmes's unusual alertness.
canon_boundaries_active: No reveal of Helen's identity or case specifics before the sitting-room.
Watson must join the case from the outset in some manner.
No modern speech or tutorial framing.
freeform_risk_areas: Player attempts to refuse going downstairs altogether
Player asks for future spoilers about the case
Player tries to arm himself before Holmes mentions danger

scene_rules_layer_4.character_knowledge_limits: Holmes can deduce travel from visible clues. Helen knows her own history and danger. Watson perceives only what is before him and what is said aloud.
scene_rules_layer_4.emotional_context: Social delicacy under fear, first proof of Holmes's method, trust being earned or thinned.
canon_boundaries_active: Holmes's deduction must remain clue-anchored in ticket and mud-splashes.
Helen is genuinely terrified, not deceptive.
No romance or supernatural framing.
freeform_risk_areas: Player tries to solve the whole case immediately

resets_between_episodes.why: It is a Session 1 interview-specific social signal and does not meaningfully persist into the night operation.
The social arrangement of the sitting-room belongs to the opening consultation and gives way to field action at Stoke Moran.
The travel rush is scene-specific; by Session 2 urgency is expressed through darkness and signal timing instead.
Pending status exists only until the lamp is either shown or not shown at the opening of Session 2.
The retention image ends with Session 1 and converts into direct embodied action at Session 2 start.

persists_across_full_story.why: It defines how fully Helen cooperates, how she receives instruction, and how she later speaks of Watson and Holmes.
Watson's grasp of Roylott's financial motive shapes moral framing, explanatory richness, and later justice/discretion choices.
Preparedness with the revolver is a concrete operational state that matters throughout the vigil and aftermath confidence.
How Helen was instructed directly affects Session 2 signal cleanliness and the moral meaning of her compliance.
The session-end choice is the bridge into Session 2 and defines the opening tone, options, and Watson's stance under nocturnal pressure.
Holmes's trust in Watson as observer, moral partner, or disciplined second is one of the story's principal relationship variables.
Helen's trust governs testimony openness, signal execution, and the emotional color of rescue and farewell.
Roylott's watchfulness changes the feel of covert movement and the danger profile of the night operation.

session_close_design.resolution_prose:
You sit with Holmes at the upper window of the Crown, and the case, which all day has seemed a scattered bundle of singular objects, begins at last to draw itself into one dreadful line. Below you the avenue lies black between the hedges; beyond it the long, low house shows only a blurred edge against the night. Then Dr. Roylott’s dog-cart grates upon the stones, the gate clanks, and his great figure passes into the darkness of Stoke Moran. A little later a lamp shines out, sharp and steady, in the middle window. It is Helen’s signal, and with it the day’s inquiry ceases to be conjecture and becomes action.

Holmes leans forward, his fingers together, and in a few grave sentences sets the true facts in order: the ventilator that opens where no ventilator should, the dummy bell-rope hanging within reach of the pillow, the bed clamped fast beneath it, the saucer of milk, the looped lash. You do not yet see the living instrument, but you see the design. A subtle and horrible crime stands plain enough before you, and the cold weight of the revolver in your pocket is answer to it.
session_close_design.hook_transition: For one instant there is rest in having the thing reduced from nightmare to method. Then the light burns on across the lawn, and Holmes turns from the window to you, for the vigil itself must now be entered in one spirit or another.

session_end_choice.choice_question: How do you commit yourself to the night's vigil with Holmes?

option_a.text: You tell Holmes that whatever waits in that room, you will go with him because Helen must not face one more night of that contrivance alone.
option_a.next_session_opens: The middle window burns like a small summons in the dark, and you cross the lawn with the loaded pistol heavy in your coat.

option_b.text: You say that you will go, but only after the signal is tested in your mind once more, for courage without precaution would merely serve Roylott's purpose.
option_b.next_session_opens: The signal shines with unnerving steadiness, and you move only after every step of the dreadful vigil has been set in order.

option_c.text: You propose that before going straight to the window you first take one circuit of the grounds, to learn whether Roylott or one of his beasts is already abroad.
option_c.next_session_opens: With the lamp newly kindled, you leave the inn not for the window at once, but for a listening circuit beneath the wandering beasts and the black trees.

session_end_choice.final_line: The light waits; so, now, does Holmes.

session_close_design.closing_moment_relationship: The selected trigger is story_position 21, the exact playable arrival point inside S1_M12 where Holmes and Watson discuss the dangers and deductions after seeing the inn-window signal. That event naturally contains the close: the clue-chain is gathered into a subtle suspicion, the primary session goal is achieved by confirming an immediate human threat and a survivable plan, and Branching Choice #4 is delivered before the vigil itself begins.
session_close_design.next_bridge_guidance: Finalize should close inside S1_M12 after the signal is seen and Holmes states the deduction chain. Hold one brief beat of earned clarity, then present Choice S1_C4 verbatim in-period voice. End on the chosen commitment posture plus the lit middle window as the carry-forward image into Session 2.

boiler_final_cut.playable_promise: Enter a real forensic detective case at Watson's side: hear a terrified woman's testimony, feel a violent stepfather's menace, and inspect a sealed murder-room where honest inspection of shutters, dummy bell-rope, ventilator, and Roylott's chamber lets you discover the hidden shape of a crime before night falls.

q1_entry_point.detail: The session starts at the first live dramatic threshold: Watson wakes to Holmes at the bedside, improper hour established, urgent client waiting below, and immediate agency follows. No passive preamble precedes the cold open.

q3_first_choice_timing.detail: Choice #1 arrives at approximately 148 words in the cold open, well within the 300-word limit.

q4_consequential_choices.detail: All four branching choices alter tracked state, NPC disposition, environmental flags, and future-session setup. S1_C1 affects Helen trust and Session 2 signal cleanliness; S1_C2 affects motive_clarity and Holmes framing; S1_C3 affects helen_plan_briefing and Session 2 transfer quality; S1_C4 sets vigil_commitment and Session 2 opening topology. These are verified against the Phase 6 consequence map and the cross-session payoff plan.

q5_stakes_within_60_seconds.detail: Before the first branch, the player knows Holmes has broken routine, a frightened young woman waits below, and joining now matters because first impressions and immediate aid may shape the case. Watson's internal stake, to be useful in a singular and urgent matter, is clear before choice.

q6_early_decision_visible_later.detail: S1_C1 has named visible later payoff: Helen's trust affects Session 1 testimony openness and Session 2 signal execution quality, with explicit next-session variants in the consequence map.

q7_breath_beat.detail: A deliberate wonder beat is placed at S1_M10, within the 17:00-19:30 range on the beat map, centered on the dummy bell-rope and the ventilator which does not ventilate. It releases pressure through clue-pleasure before the sinister inventory and moral-weight planning.

q8_moral_gray_area.detail: The genuine moral gray area is S1_C3. Values in tension: informed agency, protective steadiness, operational clarity. None of the three options is framed as objectively correct.

q9_exit_emotional_state.detail: The user exits carrying ANTICIPATION. The session ends on the player's own unresolved commitment to the vigil, with the lit middle window as the immediate carry-forward summons.

q10_talkability.detail: S1_C3 and S1_C4 are strongly talkable, especially whether Helen should be fully informed and whether Watson enters the vigil protectively, procedurally, or by irregular reconnaissance. A friend could naturally ask, 'What did you choose?'

q11_hard_ban_scan.detail: Banned voice elements appear in generated prose and guidance. Specific flags: em dashes in multiple generated lines, including entry_point_adjustment ('earliest available session moment kept — for a NOVEL source'), rubric_scores ('Body: Strong — ...'), and many scene/beat descriptions; modern/forbidden phrasing in freeform guidance such as 'consent-minded input' (S1_C3 path C), 'anti-paternal' (S1_C3 path A), and 'therapeutic' adjacent modern framing; banned AI-tell phrase appears in session_close_design resolution_prose, 'begins at last to draw itself into one dreadful line,' which is acceptable stylistically, but the hard failure is the em-dash ban from Voice Lock anchor card. Phase: Voice Lock / Phase 5-7 prose packaging. Revision: remove all em dashes from generated prose and guidance, replace modern social-process diction with period-appropriate equivalents, then rerun the hard-ban scan.

q12_trailing_simile_scan.detail: No disallowed trailing 'like [metaphor]' constructions appear in the generated action prose. The few comparisons present are either source-faithful architectural description or embedded in quoted/source-aligned material, not generic action-line simile drift.

q13_sentence_mold_scan.detail: No instances found of the banned molds 'It's not X, it's Y,' 'No X. No Y. Just Z.,' or generic contrast scaffolds of the prohibited modern type. The prose remains largely Doylean in structure.

q14_voice_authenticity.detail: Cold open clearly shows at least two signature techniques: restrained gothic/forensic scene setup through physical particulars (mantel clock, morning light, bedside stance), and Watsonian observing posture with gentlemanly domestic interruption. Random outcomes also preserve signature markers: S1_C1A uses witness-entry staging and humane observational narration; S1_C2A uses deduction from legal minutiae and explicit motive logic; S1_C4B uses procedural suspense sequencing and clipped Holmesian operational review. Attribution plausibly reads as Doyle-adjacent Watson rather than generic historical prose.

q15_fourteen_point_audit.detail: The full 14-point audit is not clean. Flags include hard-ban/em-dash violations, modern diction in freeform guidance, and narrator-compliance drift in some meta/editorial prose that steps outside runtime Watsonian texture. Phase: Voice Lock enforcement across Phases 3-7. Revision: run a dedicated voice cleanup pass on all generated prose artifacts, especially editorial-facing prose that may be surfaced or reused, then regenerate the 14-point audit until all 14 points pass.

q16_diction_fingerprint.detail: Watson's internal voice generally matches the author's diction patterns: formal register, exact nouns, clue-bearing objects, restrained moral coloring. Holmes, Helen, and Roylott also maintain distinct fingerprints consistent with Voice Lock, with Holmes clipped and evidentiary, Helen decorous and fearful, and Roylott abrupt and bullying.

fourteen_point_audit_results.location: Multiple generated prose fields contain em dashes, including entry_point_diagnosis.rubric_scores, entry_point_adjustment, session_architecture beat descriptions, and session_close_design prose.

Some generated editorial/session-support prose steps outside second-person present Watsonian runtime stance, especially in explanatory packaging and close-design prose intended to guide finalization.

q17_canon_integrity.detail: No branch or outcome breaks Doyle canon. The rational explanation remains intact, the room architecture is preserved, the snake is withheld until Session 2, and Watson cannot abandon Holmes or solve the case early.

q18_character_truth.detail: NPC behavior remains canon-faithful. Holmes stays cool and evidentiary under threat, Helen remains terrified but coherent, and Roylott is openly bullying and violent rather than suavely manipulative.

q19_world_reactivity.detail: World reactivity is active and visible. NPC trust shifts, Holmes explanatory openness, Roylott suspicion, environmental cue emphasis, and Session 2 opening variants are all explicitly tied to player behavior through named triggers such as RT_HELEN_TRUST_SIGNAL_CLEAN, RT_HOLMES_EXPLAINS_FULLER_IF_FORENSIC_PATTERN, and RT_ROYLOTT_ALERT_COMPOUNDS_NOISE.

q20_persistent_state_consistency.detail: State changes specified in choice design are consistently reflected in the consequence map. Core flags such as helen_trusts_baker_street_help, motive_clarity, watson_revolver, helen_plan_briefing, vigil_commitment, and roylott_suspicion_level are carried forward coherently.

q21_world_noticed_signals.detail: Significant persistent state changes have in-world acknowledgments written in Phase 5. Signals are subtle, physical, and in voice: Helen's posture loosens, Holmes grows brisker, the room's energy changes, the plan settles into objects, and the lawn becomes contested ground.

q22_social_echo_defining_lines.detail: Each of the four branching choices has three defining lines, one per path, all under 20 words, provocative, and non-spoiling. They are voice-compatible and curiosity-generating.

The map says courage_vs_caution should be introduced in Session 2, but this session uses it as Session 1's end hook, which is acceptable structurally; the actual failure is that S1_C1 labels a preparatory question as 'chaotic' where it reads more cautious/procedural than law-breaking, and S1_C4's options skew toward neutral/lawful caution with the 'chaotic' option functioning as prudent recon rather than true irregular boldness. Phase: Phase 5 choice alignment labeling. Revision: recalibrate alignment labels and option framing so each branch more clearly spans lawful/neutral/chaotic in behavior, not merely in tone.

scene_card.title: A Quarter-Past Seven
scene_card.treatment: Cold-open bedroom threshold at a quarter-past seven. Watson wakes to Holmes fully dressed by the bed; a frightened young lady waits below. One embodied choice: how to enter the case.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Ground the player in Watson's body and habit, establish the improper hour and pressing client, and land a posture-setting first choice within a few turns.
scene_card.player_desire: Understand what is wrong and decide how to meet it.
scene_card.live_pressure: An agitated client waits below at daybreak; first impressions will be formed with or without you.
scene_card.opening_image: Thin morning light on the mantel clock reading a quarter-past seven; Holmes, already fully dressed, stands over your bed with that quiet alertness which means some singular business is afoot.
player_affordances: Rise at once with human sympathy
Dress with professional composure to hear facts first
Pause Holmes for one precise question about the visitor before descending
Ask Holmes about the hour or the client
Observe the thin morning light and mantel clock
canon_must_keep: It is a quarter-past seven, an hour Holmes is seldom astir
A young lady in considerable excitement insists on seeing Holmes in the sitting-room below
Watson is Holmes's intimate friend and habitual companion who follows cases from the outset
allowed_variance: Watson's exact tone of surprise/resentment
Which posture the player chooses and how it is voiced
Whether Watson asks a clarifying question
forbidden_expansions: Do not reveal Helen's name, Stoke Moran, Julia, Roylott, the whistle, or the bruises
No supernatural framing
No modern colloquial speech
source_extracts: "Very sorry to knock you up, Watson," said he, "but it's the common lot this morning."
"No; a client. It seems that a young lady has arrived in a considerable state of excitement, who insists upon seeing me."
"My dear fellow, I would not miss it for anything."
scene_card.exit_condition: The central pressure resolves when Watson has committed to (or pointedly deferred) joining Holmes downstairs, his entering posture established, so the scene can hand off to the sitting-room.
scene_card.next_bridge: With his posture chosen, Watson descends the stair beside Holmes toward the sitting-room where the veiled visitor waits.

scene_card.title: It Is Fear, It Is Terror
scene_card.treatment: The sitting-room. A lady in black rises from the window; her shivering is fear, not cold. Holmes demonstrates the return-ticket and mud deduction, and invites her to lay the case before them.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Deliver first proof of the detective promise through observed deduction and earn Helen's trust in proportion to the chosen posture.
scene_card.player_desire: Take the measure of this frightened woman and see whether Holmes's method is real.
scene_card.live_pressure: A terrified stranger is on the edge of breaking; how she is received shapes how freely she will speak.
scene_card.opening_image: A lady in black, heavily veiled, rises from the window-seat; her gloved hands tremble in the firelight though the morning is not cold.
player_affordances: Reassure Helen or hold professional reserve
Notice details of her appearance (grey-shot hair, hunted eyes)
React with admiration to Holmes's deduction
Prompt Holmes or Helen to begin
Offer coffee or the fire
canon_must_keep: "It is fear, Mr. Holmes. It is terror."
Holmes deduces the dog-cart drive and morning train from the return ticket and seven mud-splashes
Holmes takes genuine interest and pledges the same care he gave Mrs. Farintosh
allowed_variance: Depth of Watson's reassurance based on M01 posture
Order of the deduction beats
Whether the case-book/Farintosh detail is surfaced or left as optional lore
forbidden_expansions: Do not yet give Julia's death account or the family history
No mystical framing of the deduction; keep it clue-anchored
No romance subplotting
source_extracts: "It is not cold which makes me shiver," said the woman in a low voice
"The left arm of your jacket is spattered with mud in no less than seven places... There is no vehicle save a dog-cart which throws up mud in that way"
"before whom you can speak as freely as before myself"
scene_card.exit_condition: Resolves when Helen is settled and reassured enough to begin her account, her trust calibrated to how the player received her.
scene_card.next_bridge: Steadied enough to speak, Helen draws a breath and begins the history of Stoke Moran and the man who rules it.

scene_card.title: The Roylotts of Stoke Moran
scene_card.treatment: Helen's account of Stoke Moran and Roylott, delivered as choosable probes: the ruined Saxon family, the Calcutta doctor who beat his butler to death, the violent temper, the cheetah and baboon, the isolated joyless household. Ends on the mention of Julia's death.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Convert front-loaded family history into interactive testimony where the player's questions (intuition vs procedure) shape which motive and menace threads are drawn out.
scene_card.player_desire: Learn who Roylott is and why this household is dangerous.
scene_card.live_pressure: The backstory is long and could smother momentum; the player must mine what matters before dread cools.
scene_card.opening_image: Helen sits forward in the firelight, her prematurely grey hair and worn face testifying to years of strain as she speaks of an ancient family reduced to one mortgaged house.
player_affordances: Probe Roylott's past (Calcutta, the butler, the prison term)
Ask about the will and the sisters' finances
Ask about the animals and the gipsies
Follow procedure with pointed factual questions or follow intuition toward the ominous
Note Helen's prematurely grey hair as evidence of the household's strain
canon_must_keep: Roylott is the last of an ancient Saxon family reduced to a mortgaged Stoke Moran house
He trained in Calcutta, beat his native butler to death, and served prison time
He keeps a free-roaming cheetah and baboon and consorts with wandering gipsies
The mother's bequest passes to Roylott while the daughters reside, with sums on marriage
allowed_variance: How much history the player draws out vs leaves as optional lore
Order of probes
Whether financial detail is deep or deferred to M07
forbidden_expansions: Do not narrate Julia's death scene here (that is M04)
No invented Roylott dialogue
Keep exposition to what the player elicits; do not dump the whole ledger unprompted
source_extracts: "the Roylotts of Stoke Moran, on the western border of Surrey"
"he beat his native butler to death and narrowly escaped a capital sentence"
"he has at this moment a cheetah and a baboon, which wander freely over his grounds"
scene_card.exit_condition: Resolves when the player has drawn out enough of Roylott's character and the household's peril, and Helen turns toward the subject of her sister's death.
scene_card.next_bridge: Her voice lowering, Helen comes at last to the night her sister died, and the account darkens into the fatal room.

scene_card.title: The Speckled Band
scene_card.treatment: Julia's last night, breathed at full length: the whistle at three a.m., the smell of cigars, the locked doors, the wild stormy night, the scream, the low whistle and metallic clang, Julia swaying into the corridor and dying with 'the speckled band.' Then Holmes's inquest probing establishes the sealed room and his 'deep waters' dissatisfaction.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Let the session's core dread land unhurried, then hand the player active forensic inquiry into the locked-room facts.
scene_card.player_desire: Grasp exactly how Julia died and why the room seems impenetrable.
scene_card.live_pressure: The account is harrowing and the facts refuse an ordinary explanation; the puzzle tightens as each escape route is sealed.
scene_card.opening_image: Helen relives the wild stormy night: a low clear whistle in the silence, a metallic clang, and her sister swaying into the corridor to gasp of a speckled band before she died.
player_affordances: Press Helen for precise details of the whistle and clang
Ask whether she could swear to what she heard
Probe the coroner's findings on door, shutters, walls, floor, chimney, and poison
Ask what 'the speckled band' might mean
React to Holmes's dissatisfaction
canon_must_keep: Julia dies gasping "It was the band! The speckled band!" pointing toward the Doctor's room
A low whistle and a metallic clang were heard on the fatal night
The room was sealed: fastened door, barred shutters, solid walls and floor, staple-barred chimney; no poison found
Holmes calls these "very deep waters" and is not satisfied by the gipsy explanation
allowed_variance: How much inquest detail the player elicits
Order of questioning
Whether the charred match/match-box detail is surfaced now or noted lightly
forbidden_expansions: Do not reveal the snake, ventilator theory, or clamped bed yet
No graphic gore; render death through Julia's convulsions, pallor, and cry
No supernatural resolution of the whistle
source_extracts: "Oh, my God! Helen! It was the band! The speckled band!"
"the door had been fastened upon the inner side, and the windows were blocked by old-fashioned shutters with broad iron bars"
"These are very deep waters," said he; "pray go on with your narrative."
scene_card.exit_condition: Resolves when the death account and the sealed-room facts are fully surfaced and the locked-room impossibility is felt as an open question.
scene_card.next_bridge: As the impossibility settles, Helen confesses she now sleeps in that very room, and the danger turns from history to the present hour.

scene_card.title: The Bruised Wrist
scene_card.treatment: Testimony's close. Helen reveals she now sleeps in the death chamber and heard the whistle last night. Holmes exposes the five livid bruises on her wrist; the player weighs protection against exposure. Helen leaves re-veiled; Holmes and Watson agree the case demands a same-day trip, ending on the door bursting open.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Spike urgency with renewed peril and the bruise reveal, land a protection-vs-exposure pressure, and commit to Stoke Moran that day.
scene_card.player_desire: Protect Helen and settle whether to act now or gather more first.
scene_card.live_pressure: Helen is already back in the fatal bed and heard the herald of death last night; the danger is immediate and personal.
scene_card.opening_image: Holmes gently draws back the frill of black lace at Helen's wrist to reveal five little livid spots, the marks of four fingers and a thumb printed on the white skin.
player_affordances: React to the bruise reveal with anger, gentleness, or restraint
Urge caution to shield Helen from Roylott's suspicion, or press for speed
Confirm the plan to visit Stoke Moran that day
Reassure Helen before she departs
Weigh the theory with Holmes
canon_must_keep: Helen now sleeps in Julia's room due to 'repairs' and heard the low whistle last night
Five livid finger-and-thumb marks are printed on Helen's wrist
Holmes and Watson resolve to see over the rooms that day while Roylott is in town
The scene ends on the door being suddenly dashed open
allowed_variance: How the player frames protection vs exposure
Depth of the theory discussion (compress per guidance)
Watson's emotional register at the bruises
forbidden_expansions: Do not resolve the full theory (that is the vigil setup)
No lurid dwelling on the bruises; keep it forensic
Do not let Watson out-deduce Holmes
source_extracts: "I suddenly heard in the silence of the night the low whistle which had been the herald of her own death."
Five little livid spots, the marks of four fingers and a thumb, were printed upon the white wrist.
"It is precisely for that reason that we are going to Stoke Moran this day... But what in the name of the devil!"
scene_card.exit_condition: Resolves when Helen has departed reassured, the same-day trip is committed, and the door bursts open to interrupt the pair.
scene_card.next_bridge: The door is dashed suddenly open, and an enormous man fills the frame, transferring the danger from testimony to the room itself.

scene_card.title: The Bent Poker
scene_card.treatment: Midpoint intensification. Roylott fills the doorway, demands what Helen has said, and is met by Holmes's bland civility about crocuses and draughts. He insults, threatens, and bends the steel poker before storming out; Holmes calmly straightens it again.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Make the antagonist's menace physically present and let the player choose a posture under direct threat, then release the tension with Holmes's quiet answer.
scene_card.player_desire: Stand your ground without provoking catastrophe, and take Roylott's measure.
scene_card.live_pressure: An enormous, uncontrollable man is threatening bodily harm in the room, having traced Helen.
scene_card.opening_image: A huge man in top-hat and frock-coat fills the doorway, hunting-crop swinging, his great yellow bird-of-prey face turning from one of you to the other.
player_affordances: Support Holmes's cool deflection or move to physically interpose
Answer Roylott with defiance or hold silence
Observe his dress, bird-of-prey features, and the bent poker
Show concern that Helen was traced
React to Holmes straightening the poker
canon_must_keep: Roylott is enormous, dressed in top-hat, frock-coat, gaiters, carrying a hunting-crop, with bird-of-prey features
Holmes answers provocation with bland understatement (weather, crocuses, draught) and does not become heated
Roylott bends the poker with his hands and threatens Holmes before leaving
Holmes straightens the poker afterward
allowed_variance: Watson's degree of physical readiness
Exact insults Roylott hurls (meddler, busybody, Jack-in-office)
Whether Watson speaks or stays silent
forbidden_expansions: Holmes must not rant or match aggression
No physical brawl beyond the poker display
Do not reveal the murder method
source_extracts: "It is a little cold for the time of the year," said Holmes.
"I am a dangerous man to fall foul of! See here." ... he seized the poker, and bent it into a curve
"When you go out close the door, for there is a decided draught."
scene_card.exit_condition: Resolves when Roylott has stormed out, the threat has been weathered without escalation, and Holmes has answered with the straightened poker.
scene_card.next_bridge: With Roylott gone and the poker straightened, Holmes sets out to learn the man's true motive, returning near one o'clock with the figures in hand.

scene_card.title: An Excellent Argument
scene_card.treatment: Holmes returns near one o'clock with the will worked out: the income falls, each daughter's marriage would cripple Roylott, proving the strongest motive. He arms Watson with the Eley's No. 2 and calls the cab for Waterloo.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Deliver motive clarity (evidence vs speed) and arm the player, converting suspicion into a case with a why and a weapon.
scene_card.player_desire: Understand what Roylott stands to lose and be ready for danger.
scene_card.live_pressure: Roylott now knows they are interested; there is no time for dawdling.
scene_card.opening_image: Holmes returns near one o'clock, a sheaf of notes in hand and the will figures clear in his mind, and lays the revolver within your reach.
player_affordances: Ask Holmes to explain the will figures
Weigh whether the motive is proof enough or requires the estate visit
Take up the revolver
Voice concern for Helen's imprudence in being traced
Decide how cautiously to frame the operation

Roylott has the strongest motive to prevent his stepdaughters' marriages

Watson's reaction to arming himself
Whether the Doctors' Commons errand is mentioned
forbidden_expansions: Do not reveal the snake or apparatus

Keep the aphorism about doctors-turned-criminals for the vigil setup

"each daughter can claim an income of £250, in case of marriage"
"An Eley's No. 2 is an excellent argument with gentlemen who can twist steel pokers into knots."
scene_card.exit_condition: Resolves when the motive is understood, Watson is armed, and the pair set out for Waterloo.
scene_card.next_bridge: Armed and resolved, the pair take the train from Waterloo into Surrey, the spring country giving way to the grey gables of Stoke Moran.

scene_card.title: Stoke Moran
scene_card.treatment: Compressed travel montage into an arrival room: Surrey lanes and the first grey-gabled sight of Stoke Moran, the stile, and the architect cover story; Helen meets them joyful that Roylott is away till evening. scene_card.player_desire: Reach the house and begin inspecting before Roylott can return.
scene_card.live_pressure: The inspection window is narrow; Roylott has already traced Helen and could learn of the visit.
scene_card.opening_image: Across the Surrey lanes the grey lichen-blotched gables of Stoke Moran rise against the sweet promise of spring, a strange contrast to the sinister quest that brings you.
player_affordances: Take in the spring-vs-sinister contrast and the mansion's gables
Confirm the architect cover story
Greet Helen and confirm Roylott's absence
Choose a cautious stealthy approach or a bolder one
Reassure Helen about locking herself in and the Harrow fallback

scene_card.title: The Barred Shutters
scene_card.treatment: The exterior and shutters. Grey lichen-blotched stone, two crab-claw wings, the ruined wing, the modern block, the suspicious scaffolding with no workmen. Holmes examines the windows; Helen bars a shutter and Holmes cannot force it, the hinges solid iron. The 'repairs' were an excuse to move Helen.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Give the player embodied forensic play on the building's exterior, discovering that the sealed-room barrier is genuine and the room-move was contrived.
scene_card.player_desire: Test whether an intruder could ever breach the shutters.
scene_card.live_pressure: Every honest test closes a route; the impossibility deepens even as time runs.
scene_card.opening_image: The building of grey, lichen-blotched stone spreads its two curving wings like the claws of a crab, with scaffolding against an end wall that shows no sign of workmen.
player_affordances: Examine each wing, the ruined roof, the modern block, and the scaffolding
Note the absence of workmen and the needless end-wall repair
Have Helen bar the shutter and try to force it
Inspect hinges and look for a knife-slit
Reason aloud about corridor windows being too narrow
canon_must_keep: The barred shutters cannot be forced; hinges are solid iron in massive masonry; no slit for a knife
The end-wall repairs were a needless excuse to move Helen into the middle room
Corridor windows are too narrow to pass and the doors were locked, making the rooms unapproachable from that side
allowed_variance: Order of exterior hotspots examined
How the player voices the 'excuse' realization
Depth of scaffolding suspicion
forbidden_expansions: Do not allow any working intruder route through shutter, window, or corridor
Do not reveal the ventilator/rope apparatus yet
No supernatural entry
source_extracts: The building was of grey, lichen-blotched stone, with a high central portion and two curving wings, like the claws of a crab
"there does not seem to be any very pressing need for repairs at that end wall." ... "it was an excuse to move me from my room."
Holmes... endeavoured in every way to force the shutter open, but without success.
scene_card.exit_condition: Resolves when the shutters are proven impassable and the room-move is understood as contrived, sending the inquiry inside.
scene_card.next_bridge: The shutters proving impassable, Holmes leads you within, to the middle bedroom where Julia died and where Helen now sleeps.

scene_card.title: The Dummy Bell-Rope
scene_card.treatment: The death chamber interior. Low ceiling, gaping fireplace, worm-eaten oak panelling, the clamped narrow bed, the Wilton carpet. Holmes crawls the floor and walls, then tugs the thick bell-rope by the pillow: a dummy, not attached to any wire, fastened to a hook just above a ventilator that opens into the next room, not outdoors.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Deliver the session's central clue discovery as a room the player inhabits and inspects for several turns, surfacing the dummy rope and the ventilator-that-does-not-ventilate.
scene_card.player_desire: Find what is wrong with this innocent-looking room.
scene_card.live_pressure: The clues are subtle and the answer is nearly in reach; missing them leaves Helen in the fatal bed tonight.
scene_card.opening_image: A low-ceilinged chamber of worm-eaten oak panelling and a gaping fireplace; a thick bell-rope hangs by the pillow, its tassel resting on the clamped narrow bed.

scene_card.title: Roylott's Chamber
scene_card.treatment: Roylott's chamber. Plain furnishings, a shelf of technical books, and the principal objects: a large iron safe with a saucer of milk on top, a wooden chair bolted to the wall bearing signs of being stood upon, and a small dog lash curled and tied into a loop of whipcord on the bed corner.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Complete the apparatus discovery through inspectable objects, letting the player assemble the ominous inventory without Holmes naming the solution.
scene_card.player_desire: Read the meaning in Roylott's strange possessions.
scene_card.live_pressure: Time in the enemy's own room is dangerous, and the objects hint at a method too subtle to name aloud.

scene_card.next_bridge: The sinister inventory complete, Holmes leads you out to the lawn, where the plan for the night must be laid before darkness falls.

scene_card.title: The Signal in the Dark
scene_card.treatment: Final cash-out. On the lawn Holmes gravely warns Helen her life depends on compliance and lays out the signal plan: feign a headache, when Roylott retires open the shutters and set the lamp as a signal, then withdraw to the old room. From the Crown Inn they watch Roylott drive past and a light spring up. In gathering darkness Holmes assembles the clues — ventilator inferred from the cigar smell, the clamped bed, the dummy rope — and Watson commits to the dangerous vigil.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Assemble the session's discovered clues into dread and a plan, land the courage-vs-caution commitment to the night, and close on the promise cashed out: real detection made playable.
scene_card.player_desire: Turn the clues into a survivable plan and steel yourself for the night.
scene_card.live_pressure: Night is falling on a subtle, horrible crime; the vigil must be arranged and joined before it is too late.
scene_card.opening_image: On the lawn with the grey house behind you and evening drawing on, Holmes speaks more gravely than his wont, laying out the lamp-signal plan while Helen stands deadly pale before you.

scene_card.exit_condition: Resolves when the signal plan is set, the trap is confirmed by the appearing light, the clue-chain is assembled into recognition of a subtle crime, and Watson has committed to the night vigil, closing the session on the edge of the wait.

entry_point.chosen_moment: Event 22: the signal light appears in the middle window and Holmes and Watson must leave the inn at once for the Manor House.
entry_point.rubric_scores:
Body: Strong. The player can begin in the body at once, rising from waiting, feeling the night air and the sudden shock of movement after suspense.
Tension: Strong. The signal means the plan is live and danger to Helen is no longer theoretical.
Threshold: Strong. This is Watson's own crossing from watcher to participant, leaving safety for the night operation.
Exposition debt: Low. Only a few load-bearing facts are needed: Helen is in danger, the light is the arranged signal, and stealth is essential.
Core-stakes proximity: Very high. This is the direct launch into the vigil whose purpose is to keep Helen alive.
entry_point.entry_point_adjustment: moved forward to: Event 22 — because for a NOVEL source the earlier material belongs to Session 1, and this is the first live threshold in Session 2 that places the player in immediate embodied danger with a meaningful choice inside 300 words.
entry_point.cut_point: The cold open ends just before Holmes and Watson commit to their exact approach across the grounds, handing to the Phase 4 SETUP beat of the dark advance toward Stoke Moran.

protagonist_introduction.identity_reveal_approach: Body first through the strain of waiting at the inn and the sudden physical start when the signal appears. The name comes at the moment Holmes addresses you under operational pressure. Role is conveyed through reflex: you rise with him, prepare to follow into danger, and are already the trusted companion expected to act, not merely observe. One loaded detail: the revolver, not yet drawn but already part of your readiness.
protagonist_introduction.reveal_lines: "That is our signal," says Holmes, springing to his feet. "Come, Watson; there is not an instant to lose."
protagonist_introduction.resume_dump_check: No stacked-label exposition is used. Watson's identity as Holmes's intimate friend, medical man, and armed companion is delivered as present-tense operational fact through Holmes's address, the shared plan, and Watson's practiced readiness.

situation_stakes_world.established: You are at the Crown Inn opposite Stoke Moran, late at night. The pressing now is that Helen's lamp, the arranged sign, has appeared, which means she has done her part and the window is open for your approach. Two active world rules matter at once: stealth is life, because any sound may ruin the plan, and the threat comes from inside a house that has already killed once. The stake is immediate: if you fail in caution or speed, Helen may die before dawn.
situation_stakes_world.deferred: The full mechanism of the attack, the exact significance of the ventilator and dummy bell-rope, Holmes's revised theory, and the final moral explanation are all withheld for later beats.

first_choice_spec.setup_prose: Across the dark road the middle window burns with a single steady light. Holmes is upon his feet in an instant, and his hand is already on your sleeve. Beyond the trees lies the house where one woman died in terror and another waits this night upon your nerve and his judgment.
first_choice_spec.threshold_stake: Whether you enter the night operation in a posture of stealth, haste, or direct intervention, which turns on Helen's immediate survival and Watson's core threat of failing Holmes and a woman under protection.
first_choice_spec.question: How do you mean to go to that house?
first_choice_spec.option_1: You urge that you go at once and as silently as possible, trusting the arranged signal and Holmes's plan.
first_choice_spec.option_2: You press Holmes to pause one moment and make certain that the light is truly Helen's and not a trap set for you.
first_choice_spec.option_3_unexpected: You propose that instead of creeping straight to the window, you first circle the grounds to learn whether Roylott or one of his beasts is already abroad.
first_choice_spec.not_a_tutorial: This choice launches the entire night operation, defines Watson's risk posture at the instant Helen's life depends upon it, and directly shapes the danger profile of the vigil rather than warming up on a side encounter.
