entry_point_diagnosis.cold_open:
The night air has grown raw with waiting, and your limbs are stiff from the long vigil at the inn window. Across the dark road, beyond the black mass of trees, a single bright light springs out and burns steady in the middle casement of Stoke Moran.

Holmes is upon his feet before you have fairly drawn breath. "That is our signal," says Holmes, springing to his feet. "Come, Watson; there is not an instant to lose." At the name you are moving also, for this is no longer a case discussed by lamplight, but a woman shut in with the same danger which killed her sister. The light means that Miss Stoner has done her part. If Roylott has not forestalled us, the window stands ready; if he has, every minute is of consequence, and every sound may be fatal.

Across the dark road the middle window burns with a single steady light. Holmes is upon his feet in an instant, and his hand is already on your sleeve. Beyond the trees lies the house where one woman died in terror and another waits this night upon your nerve and his judgment. How do you mean to go to that house?
entry_point_diagnosis.emotional_promise: The emotional promise of this cold open is: resolve. A user arrives feeling apprehensive and wanting to act.
entry_point_diagnosis.freeform_input_hint: The light is up, but the trees may tell their own tale.
entry_point_diagnosis.editorial_diagnosis: I cut everything before the signal because Session 2's playable pressure does not begin with retrospective explanation, but with the arranged sign appearing and forcing immediate action. Event 22 is the correct entry for this session because it is the first live threshold in which Watson is bodily present, under pressure, and able to decide something that matters at once. I did not move forward to Event 23 or 24 merely because the baboon scare or the bedroom setup are more vivid. Event 22 already contains the essential architecture of agency: a signal, a plan going live, a vulnerable person depending on you, and a crossing from safety into danger. Starting later would cut the protagonist's first agency in Session 2, namely how Watson commits himself to the operation the instant the signal appears. What was cut from the source before this point was not part of this session allocation, but I still had to restore a few essential facts in compressed form: that the lamp is Helen's signal, that you are waiting at the Crown Inn to act on it, that Helen faces Julia's fate, and that stealth is critical. These are woven in as present pressure rather than backstory summary. I also cut the walk to the grounds, the breach in the wall, and the baboon encounter from the cold open, not from the session, because they belong in the immediate setup beat after the first choice and provide excellent downstream consequence space for the chosen risk posture. This preserves the novel's procedural suspense while ensuring the first branching choice arrives within the required word count and is tied to the core stake of Helen's survival.

boiler_draft.playable_promise: You are Watson on a live night operation: cross the dark grounds, hold a silent vigil in absolute darkness beside a sleeping trap, and be present at the instant Holmes's decisive strike turns the hidden killer back upon its master — every sense strained, every sound potentially fatal.

session_budget_decision.budget_reasoning: The session target of 23 minutes is adopted unchanged. I chose 10 moments inside the 9-12 range because the guidance demands that the climax breathe: the signal, grounds approach, darkness wait, oil smell, whistle/strike, and reveal each require deliberate temporal stretch and must not be collapsed into one another. Ten moments let me give discrete breathing rooms to the darkness (115), the oil gleam (116), the strike/shriek (117), and the speckled-band reveal (119) while compressing the concise beats the guidance flags — the departure walk (112 folds into the grounds approach 113), Holmes's revised conclusions (121) and the evidence/attack explanation (122) fold into a single debrief moment. This keeps the felt time slow across the vigil while keeping the moment count honest to the room concept.

event_role_map.why: The signal appearing and the departure into the night is the Entry Point and the first live threshold: Watson commits to the operation's risk posture (stealth/haste/vigilance) at the instant Helen's survival goes from theoretical to immediate. A load-bearing identity/commitment pressure.

The grounds crossing with the distorted-child (baboon) scare is a genuinely inhabitable room: movement under threat, noise discipline, ambient animal menace, and Holmes's vice-grip startle reveal relationship under strain. Guidance marks it must_compress, so it is concise but still playable.

Staging the vigil — shoes off, shutters closed, revolver, cane, matches, candle placed, lamp extinguished — is a rich procedural room where the player configures the trap and chooses proof-vs-protection. Must-breathe.

The dreadful vigil in absolute darkness is the emotional core of felt time: sensory deprivation, the clock striking, the cheetah's whine. This must breathe as its own inhabited room where nothing happens yet everything is at stake.

The gleam at the ventilator and the growing smell of burning oil and heated metal is one strong sensory image that breaks the darkness — a short, sharp playable beat of dawning wrongness. Must-breathe, given its own moment.

The soft steam-jet hiss, Holmes springing up, the match, the furious lashing at the bell-pull, and the horrible shriek is the violent reversal — the session's central pressure resolving in a room the player inhabits under maximum tension. Choice of decisive action vs patient observation lives here.

The decision to take the pistol and enter Roylott's room is a short duty-vs-self-preservation crossing into the aftermath. Guidance marks it must_compress, so it is a brief threshold beat rather than a full room.

The crime-scene tableau — Roylott dead, dressing-gown, dog-whip, open safe, and the speckled band that rears into a living snake — is the singular reveal. Must-breathe as an examinable horror room where the mystery's solution becomes visible.
Holmes naming the swamp adder, speaking the moral aphorism, and noosing the snake into the iron safe is the decisive containment — a room of resolution and forensic action. Must-breathe.

Holmes's revised conclusions (insufficient data, ventilator, dummy rope, clamped bed, snake bridge) are the required rational retrospective synthesis. Folded with 122 into a single debrief room; must_compress so delivered as interactive Q&A rather than a monologue dump.

The evidence account (chair-standing, safe, saucer of milk, whipcord, metallic clang) and Holmes confirming he lit the light and attacked, driving the snake back to turn upon Roylott, completes the moral shape. Compressed into the same debrief; recoil causality is the load-bearing canon.

source_extracts: How shall I ever forget that dreadful vigil? I could not hear a sound, not even the drawing of a breath... The shutters cut off the least ray of light, and we waited in absolute darkness.

once at our very window a long drawn catlike whine, which told us that the cheetah was indeed at liberty... Twelve struck, and one and two and three, and still we sat waiting silently for whatever might befall.
moment_drafts.exit_condition_draft: The pressure resolves when the long empty wait has been fully felt and the darkness is broken by the first sign of movement in the adjacent room.

moment_drafts.treatment: The first wrongness. A momentary gleam of light shows in the direction of the ventilator, then vanishes, succeeded by a strong smell of burning oil and heated metal — someone next door has lit a dark-lantern. A gentle sound of movement, then silence, and the smell grows stronger through the strained half-hour.
moment_drafts.runtime_goal: Deliver one strong sensory image that pierces the darkness and signals the trap is being sprung, intensifying dread at the session midpoint.
moment_drafts.player_desire: To understand what is happening on the other side of the wall without betraying your presence.
moment_drafts.live_pressure: Something is moving in Roylott's room; the smell and gleam mean the attack has begun, but you cannot yet see the danger.

I heard a gentle sound of movement, and then all was silent once more, though the smell grew stronger.
moment_drafts.exit_condition_draft: The pressure resolves when the meaning of the gleam and smell has fully registered as imminent threat and the room falls back into taut silence awaiting the next sound.

moment_drafts.treatment: The reversal. A very gentle soothing sound, like a small jet of steam from a kettle. Holmes springs from the bed, strikes a match, and lashes furiously at the bell-pull, yelling 'You see it, Watson?' The sudden glare blinds Watson; a low clear whistle sounds; Holmes's face is deadly pale with horror and loathing. Then the most horrible cry breaks from the night and swells and dies.
moment_drafts.runtime_goal: Play the violent, disorienting climax of the vigil where decisive action meets Watson's blinded, partial perception, resolving the night's central pressure.
moment_drafts.player_desire: To see the thing Holmes lashes at and act in the sudden chaos of light and sound.
moment_drafts.live_pressure: The attack is happening now; Holmes strikes at something unseen and a terrible cry answers — you must react blind, in an instant.

his face was deadly pale and filled with horror and loathing... there broke from the silence of the night the most horrible cry to which I have ever listened.
moment_drafts.exit_condition_draft: The pressure resolves when the strike is spent, the cry has died into silence, and the pair stand gazing at each other knowing something decisive has happened next door.

moment_drafts.treatment: The crossing to the aftermath. 'What can it mean?' Holmes answers that it is all over, and perhaps for the best. He lights the lamp, leads down the corridor, knocks twice at the chamber door without reply, then turns the handle. Watson follows at his heels with the cocked pistol. Concise per compress guidance — a taut threshold beat.
moment_drafts.runtime_goal: Move the player from the vigil room into Roylott's chamber under duty-vs-self-preservation pressure, pistol readied, into the unknown behind the door.

source_extracts: "It means that it is all over," Holmes answered. "And perhaps, after all, it is for the best. Take your pistol, and we will enter Dr. Roylott's room."
Twice he struck at the chamber door without any reply from within. Then he turned the handle and entered, I at his heels, with the cocked pistol in my hand.
moment_drafts.exit_condition_draft: The pressure resolves when the door is open and the pair stand on the threshold of Roylott's lit room, about to see what waits.

moment_drafts.treatment: The crime-scene tableau. The dark-lantern's half-open shutter throws a beam on the ajar iron safe. Roylott sits in his grey dressing-gown, bare ankles, red Turkish slippers, the dog-whip across his lap, chin cocked upward, eyes fixed in a rigid stare. Round his brow a peculiar yellow band with brownish speckles — which begins to move, rearing the squat diamond head of a snake. 'The band! the speckled band!'
moment_drafts.runtime_goal: Let the player inspect the deadly tableau and witness the singular reveal as the speckled band resolves into the living murder weapon.
moment_drafts.player_desire: To read the scene, confirm Roylott's fate, and comprehend the horror of the band.

moment_drafts.treatment: Containment and moral verdict. Holmes cries 'It is a swamp adder — the deadliest snake in India,' notes Roylott died within ten seconds, and speaks the maxim that violence recoils upon the violent and the schemer falls into his own pit. He draws the dog-whip from the dead man's lap, nooses the reptile's neck, carries it at arm's length, and thrusts it into the iron safe, closing it.
moment_drafts.runtime_goal: Resolve the immediate danger through Holmes's decisive containment and deliver the moral shape of the ending while the player acts alongside him.
moment_drafts.player_desire: To see the deadly thing safely trapped and Miss Stoner's rescue set in motion.
moment_drafts.live_pressure: A venomous swamp adder is loose in the room and must be secured before anyone can be safe.

Watch or assist as Holmes nooses the snake with the dog-whip
React to the swamp adder's identification

source_extracts: "It is a swamp adder!" cried Holmes; "the deadliest snake in India. He has died within ten seconds of being bitten. Violence does, in truth, recoil upon the violent, and the schemer falls into the pit which he digs for another."
throwing the noose round the reptile's neck he drew it from its horrid perch and, carrying it at arm's length, threw it into the iron safe, which he closed upon it.
moment_drafts.exit_condition_draft: The pressure resolves when the swamp adder is locked in the safe and the danger is contained, freeing the pair to turn to Helen's rescue and explanation.

moment_drafts.treatment: The debrief and final synthesis. Holmes lays out the rational retrospective chain as interactive Q&A: his erroneous first conclusion from insufficient data (the gipsies, the word 'band'), his reconsideration when danger could come from neither window nor door, the ventilator and dummy bell-rope, the clamped bed as a bridge for something passing through, the snake, the untraceable Eastern poison, the whistle to recall it, the milk to train it. Then the evidence (chair-standing, safe, saucer of milk, whipcord, the metallic clang of the safe door) and his admission that he lit the light and attacked, driving the snake back to turn upon its master. Compressed per guidance into one closing room.
moment_drafts.runtime_goal: Assemble the complete rational solution and moral coda through player-driven questioning, confirming the recoil causality and closing the session.
moment_drafts.player_desire: To understand exactly how the murder worked and how Holmes turned it back on Roylott.
moment_drafts.live_pressure: The night is won, but the full truth is still unspoken; Watson (and the player) must piece together how it was done.

The method is a trained venomous snake using untraceable Eastern poison, recalled by a whistle and trained with milk
Evidence: the chair for standing to reach the ventilator, the safe, the saucer of milk, the loop of whipcord, the metallic clang of the safe door closing on the snake
Holmes lit the light and attacked the snake, driving it back through the ventilator to turn upon and kill Roylott (recoil causality)

Which details are surfaced first

source_extracts: "I had... come to an entirely erroneous conclusion which shows, my dear Watson, how dangerous it always is to reason from insufficient data."

"The discovery that this was a dummy, and that the bed was clamped to the floor, instantly gave rise to the suspicion that the rope was there as a bridge for something passing through the hole and coming to the bed."

"I heard the creature hiss as I have no doubt that you did also, and I instantly lit the light and attacked it." ... "And also with the result of causing it to turn upon its master at the other side."
moment_drafts.exit_condition_draft: The pressure resolves when the full clue-to-inference chain and the recoil causality are understood, and the case is closed with Holmes's compact moral verdict — the final cash-out of the session.

setup.source_moment: Event 112 / moment S2_M01: the signal light appears in the middle window; Holmes springs up at once — “That is our signal... Come, Watson; there is not an instant to lose.”
setup.why_it_qualifies: This is the cold-open threshold and first live tension point. Location, situation, and stake are instantly legible: you are at the inn opposite Stoke Moran, Helen’s signal is up, and the operation must begin now. It satisfies the entry-point rule because it cuts directly to action under pressure, and branching choice #1 can arrive within the first 300 words as Watson commits to a risk posture.

escalation.source_moment: Events 113-116 / moments S2_M02-S2_M05: crossing the grounds past the breach and baboon scare; entering the room; Holmes’s whispered rules; the long vigil; then the ventilator gleam, oil smell, and movement next door.
escalation.why_it_qualifies: The visible goal is to enter Helen’s room unseen, endure the vigil, and catch the hidden attack in time to stop it. The clear obstacle is double: discovery by Roylott or his beasts, and ignorance of the exact method while sitting in fatal silence. These moments compound operational pressure through procedural suspense rather than exposition.

breath.source_moment: Event 113 / moment S2_M02: the hideous distorted child-like figure darts across the lawn, only for Holmes to whisper dryly, “It is a nice household... That is the baboon.”
breath.why_it_qualifies: This is the session’s release valve: a brief absurd shock amid danger, landing as dry Holmesian understatement rather than comic relief detached from menace. It preserves the author’s restrained humor and gives the player a Schell-rule reward without breaking suspense.

twist.source_moment: Events 117-118 / moments S2_M06-S2_M07: Holmes strikes at the bell-pull after the hiss; the horrible cry follows; then he says it is all over and bids Watson take the pistol and enter Roylott’s room.
twist.why_it_qualifies: The moral-weight turn is not merely the strike but the immediate decision to go into Roylott’s room after an unseen reversal. There is no correct answer in attitude: duty demands entry, but self-preservation is rational because the deadly thing may still be loose. The player must decide whether Watson enters as bold support, disciplined caution, or reluctant but dutiful witness.

resolution.source_moment: Events 119-122 / moments S2_M08-S2_M10: Roylott dead with the speckled band revealed as a snake; Holmes secures it in the safe; Holmes explains the full clue-chain and admits his strike drove it back upon its master.
resolution.why_it_qualifies: The primary arc resolves because the immediate threat to Helen is ended and the hidden method is rationally exposed. The seed for the next session is not plot continuation, since this is the final session, but the unresolved moral framing: whether the truth becomes public justice or remains a discreet private truth. The session therefore ends on the player’s own aftermath commitment rather than a mere explanatory full stop.

branching_choices.source_moment: Event 112 / moment S2_M01: the signal light appears in the middle window; Holmes springs up at once, 'That is our signal... Come, Watson; there is not an instant to lose.'
branching_choices.narrative_setup: Across the dark road the middle window burns with a single steady light. Holmes is upon his feet in an instant, and his hand is already on your sleeve. Beyond the trees lies the house where one woman died in terror and another waits this night upon your nerve and his judgment.
branching_choices.choice_question: How do you mean to go to that house?

options.label: A
options.text: You urge that you go at once and as silently as possible, trusting the arranged signal and Holmes's plan.
options.outcome: You speak low, but with decision, and Holmes answers you with a brief pressure of the hand, as one professional man acknowledging another's steadiness. A moment later you are out upon the dark road, the chill wind in your face, the one yellow light before you guiding your sombre errand. No word is wasted. At the breach in the old park wall you follow him among the trees, placing each foot with care, your revolver heavy and serviceable in your pocket. The lawn opens pale before you, the middle window beyond it, and because you have chosen silence over speculation, every faculty in you narrows to one plain duty, to reach that room unheard before the house can wake.
options.downstream_effect: The approach begins immediately, with Holmes treating you as a fully reliable operational partner and the noise profile kept low.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Watson's revolver mentally readied; no physical change.

npc_dispositions.shift: indirect reassurance +1, as the rescue proceeds without delay

options.world_noticed_signal: Holmes wastes neither praise nor correction. He moves, and the night seems to close round your shared purpose.
options.defining_line: You choose not bravery in words, but obedience under the lash of time.

options.label: B
options.text: You press Holmes to pause one moment and make certain that the light is truly Helen's and not a trap set for you.
options.outcome: Your caution is no cowardice, and Holmes does not treat it as such. He turns his eyes once more upon the middle casement, measuring its steadiness, its position, and the darkness of the neighbouring windows; then he gives the smallest nod. 'Quite so,' he whispers, and for that single instant the enterprise alters from a rush into a checked and reasoned advance. The delay is brief, but it sharpens your sense that a false light, a movement at the wrong blind, a shadow where none should be, might have sent you under a murderous hand. When at last you cross the road, you do so with the house not merely as a destination, but as a problem to be tested, and the black trees receive you accordingly.
options.downstream_effect: The approach is delayed for a brief verification, increasing evidentiary confidence while tightening the sense of possible trap.

npc_dispositions.shift: indirect anxiety +1 due to slight delay

options.world_noticed_signal: The lamp across the road burns on, unwavering and solitary. Only when its innocence has been weighed do you commit yourself to the grounds.
options.defining_line: You ask the night to prove itself before you trust it.

options.label: C
options.text: You propose that instead of creeping straight to the window, you first circle the grounds to learn whether Roylott or one of his beasts is already abroad.
options.outcome: The suggestion is a bold one, and for an instant Holmes's face, dimly seen, takes on that quick alertness with which he greets an unexpected line of action that is not wholly foolish. He inclines his head, and you sweep wider of the direct path, skirting the darker edge of the grounds where the laurels mass thickly and the broken wall gives way to open lawn. The house is no longer merely the point to be gained, but the centre of a ring of possible danger, man, cheetah, baboon, or watcher at a casement. The circuit costs you time and steadiness of nerve in equal measure, yet it yields a harsher intimacy with the place, the damp earth, the branches, the sense of a violent household breathing in the dark, just before something stirs ahead.

options.text: You place yourself and your revolver for the quickest defence of the bed, meaning to stop any threat the instant it shows itself.
options.outcome: You think first, as a doctor and a man of honour, of the sleeper who lately lay where the fixed bed now gapes pale in the darkness. The revolver is laid where your hand can close upon it at once, your chair chosen less for sight-line than for intervention, and your whole body held in readiness to rise between the peril and its victim. Holmes gives you a quick, searching look, then assents by shifting the candle stump a bare inch and leaving the rest to silence. You may miss some single point by refusing a single focus, yet you gain a harsher sense that peril may enter by movement, sound, or man.

'It means that it is all over,' he says, 'and perhaps, after all, it is for the best. Take your pistol, and we will enter Dr. Roylott's room.'
branching_choices.choice_question: When Holmes says it is all over and bids you take your pistol, do you enter at once, hold back for caution, or insist on a safer read first?

options.label: A
options.text: You go in at Holmes's heels without another instant's delay, accepting that whatever remains alive beyond that door must be faced before it can strike again.
options.outcome: You cock the pistol and close upon Holmes so nearly that the lamp throws your shadow beside his upon the corridor wall. There is danger still, beyond question, but delay itself has become a form of surrender, and you will not have it said, even in your private conscience, that you halted when the crisis had broken open. The knock goes unanswered. The handle turns. You enter with the immediate violence of the cry still sounding in memory, ready to fire if anything living springs from the chair, the safe, or the gloom beyond the lantern's beam. Such haste may expose you to the very remnant of the trap, yet it purchases the fullest witness of what waits within. If horror is there, you mean to meet it standing, not infer it from the passage.
options.downstream_effect: You witness the tableau at the earliest possible instant, increasing direct exposure and the completeness of your later account.
options.world_noticed_signal: The corridor scarcely exists for you as a place at all. It is only the short distance between decision and the opened door.
options.defining_line: You choose the room before the room can choose you.

options.label: B
options.text: You obey Holmes, but make him pause at the threshold while you cover the room carefully with the pistol before either of you commit your full weight inside.
options.outcome: Courage need not be blind to be real, and your caution here has the temper of discipline rather than fear. At the door you take your station as covering man, pistol raised, while Holmes's lamp and your own searching glance do what they may to read the first facts before a step is spent. Table, lantern, safe, chair, the outline of the seated figure, each is taken in not leisurely, but in sequence, as a surgeon might reckon instruments before touching the wound. Holmes neither hurries nor rebukes you. He knows as well as you that a deadly creature, once loosed, does not become harmless because a man has screamed. You surrender some immediacy of witness, but you preserve the chance that neither of you blunder into the final movement of a subtle and horrible crime.
options.downstream_effect: The entry slows into a controlled threshold clearance, reducing immediate risk while slightly delaying full inspection.

options.label: C
options.text: You stop Holmes one instant to listen, watch the safe and ventilator line, and judge whether the unseen danger has truly spent itself before crossing the threshold.
options.outcome: The request is brief, almost whispered, but it arrests the next step and turns the threshold itself into an instrument of inquiry. You listen for the hiss again, mark whether the safe stands merely ajar or quivers with life, and keep one eye upon the upper line where wall, ventilator, and shadow meet. Holmes gives you that instant, because he too knows the worst errors are made when men assume the event complete because the noise has ceased. The pause may cost you the first unbroken sight of Roylott's chamber as it stood after the cry; yet it honours another duty, not to rush into a death-trap merely because courage is easier to admire than prudence. When at last you cross, it is with the room already half-read as danger, not spectacle.
options.downstream_effect: The threshold becomes a last evidentiary pause, improving hazard assessment while sacrificing some immediate witness detail.

branching_choices.source_moment: Events 121-122 / moment S2_M10: Holmes reconstructs the clue-chain and Watson decides how the truth should live afterward.
branching_choices.narrative_setup: The snake is shut once more in the iron safe, Helen is to be removed to shelter, and the room's singular horror has yielded at last to a chain of true facts. Holmes, with that grave composure which follows his hardest labours, has shown you the line from ventilator to dummy bell-rope, from clamped bed to whistle, milk, and recoil. Yet explanation is not the same thing as judgment, and what is known in this chamber need not be known in the same fashion beyond it.
branching_choices.choice_question: Now that the method is known and Helen is safe, do you mean this truth for official exposure or for a quieter moral settlement?

options.label: A
options.text: You mean to press the matter toward formal account, giving authorities as full a truth as the evidence can bear, whatever scandal follows.
options.outcome: The impulse is a just one. A woman has been hunted in her bed, another murdered before her, and if the law cannot wholly punish the dead, it may at least be made to look steadily upon the method of his wickedness. Holmes hears you out with a face that does not mock the scruple, though he may doubt the practical harvest of it. The chair, the safe, the saucer of milk, the looped lash, the ventilator which does not ventilate, all stand ready as mute witnesses, yet the central agent is a snake now caged and a master already beyond the dock. To tell all is to risk noise, disbelief, and scandal for Helen; but it is also to refuse that subtle crimes should pass into mere village rumour. The morning, in this path, begins with statements.
options.downstream_effect: The aftermath turns toward official disclosure, increasing scrutiny, evidentiary pressure, and public framing of the case.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Case notes mentally committed for fuller statement.

options.world_noticed_signal: The room ceases to be merely the end of a danger and becomes the beginning of an inquiry. Even the silent objects seem to await inventory.
options.defining_line: You would have the law stare into the ventilator, however ugly the view.
options.next_session_opens: Morning finds you with Holmes before authority, the iron safe shut, the true facts harder to prove than to know.

options.label: B
options.text: You argue that Helen's safety matters more than public process, and that the dead man's own device has already passed the sternest sentence upon him.
options.outcome: There is a fierce mercy in such a conclusion, though it walks near dangerous ground. Roylott has died by the very engine he fashioned for another, and you feel no appetite to drag Helen through coroner's curiosity, county gossip, and the incredulity that often greets a subtle and horrible crime. Holmes's own maxim stands behind you, violence recoiling upon the violent, and the moral symmetry of it is hard to deny. Yet private justice has its shadows. To let the full truth sink into partial report is to trust conscience over institution, and to accept that some manifold wickedness is punished by event rather than by court. Helen, in this course, may recover the sooner; but the case-book itself acquires a graver burden, for what is spared the public must be carried accurately somewhere.
options.downstream_effect: The aftermath bends toward private moral settlement, protecting Helen from scandal while limiting official truth.

options.defining_line: You let the dead man's punishment stand, and spare the living the rest.

options.label: C
options.text: You choose a middle course, meaning to give the police enough for a workable verdict while keeping the strangest particulars from becoming Helen's lifelong burden.
options.outcome: This is the gentleman's compromise, and perhaps the most difficult to keep clean. The county police may be told what they must know, that a dangerous creature kept by a violent man turned fatally upon him, that Miss Stoner must be secured elsewhere, that no further peril remains in the house. Beyond that lies the more singular architecture of guilt, the dummy bell-rope, the ventilator, the trained return by whistle and milk, matters true enough, yet so fantastic in appearance that they may injure the witness more than they instruct the magistrate. Holmes is well suited to such calibrations, for he has never confused the whole truth with the whole statement. But moderation has its own risk, that one begins by trimming scandal and ends by trimming justice. The first report, here, is measured rather than complete.
options.downstream_effect: The case is framed as controlled partial disclosure, balancing practical verdict with protection of Helen's future reputation.

options.world_noticed_signal: The facts begin at once to separate into those fit for the police and those fit only for the case-book. Silence becomes a method, not an evasion.

emotional_choices.source_moment: Baboon scare on the lawn; Holmes whispers, 'It is a nice household... That is the baboon.'
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: The thing has gone across the lawn with writhing limbs, and Holmes's fingers still bite your wrist. Then his whisper comes, absurdly composed in the midst of danger.
emotional_choices.choice_question: How do you receive the explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: You breathe out a low incredulous laugh before mastering yourself again.
options.outcome: The laugh is no more than a breath, but it clears the first violence of the start from your chest. For an instant the monstrous household becomes not less dangerous, but more singularly human in its grotesque arrangements, and Holmes's own low amusement steadies rather than offends you. Then the need for silence returns in full, and you gather yourself at once, ashamed neither of the alarm nor of the brief relief that followed it. The lawn remains to be crossed, the window to be gained, and the absurdity of the baboon only sharpens the knowledge that worse than absurdity waits within.
options.tonal_effect: Narration admits a brief dry release before returning to taut procedure.
options.world_noticed_signal: Holmes's mouth tightens for the fraction of a second that serves him as a smile. Then both of you are grave again.

options.label: B
options.text: You swallow the fright and move on with a muttered acknowledgment.
options.outcome: You accept the explanation as one more fact to be carried, not dwelt upon. Baboon or no baboon, the matter before you is unchanged, and so you confine your reaction to the smallest sign that you have heard him. The self-command is not showy, but serviceable. It leaves the mind free for the next footfall, the next bush, the next possible movement in the dark. If the household is bizarre, it is also violent, and you treat the one as subordinate to the other. Thus the absurdity passes into inventory, and the night closes over it at once.
options.tonal_effect: Narration grows cooler and more reportorial.
options.world_noticed_signal: The grass stirs where the creature vanished, and then even that sign is gone. Only the work remains.

options.label: C
options.text: You steady yourself at once and whisper that the house grows no more inviting by explanation.
options.outcome: Your answer is low and composed, with just enough dryness in it to meet Holmes upon his own ground without forgetting the danger. The remark does not lighten the business, but it restores proportion. A baboon may explain the shape upon the lawn, yet it leaves untouched the dead girl, the waiting sister, and the murderous intelligence somewhere in the dark house before you. Holmes gives the faintest nod, as if satisfied that the startle has not mastered you. Together you resume the crossing with that compact understanding which makes speech unnecessary between tried companions.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes firmer, companionable, and quietly assured.
options.world_noticed_signal: NO SIGNAL — state change is minor

emotional_choices.source_moment: Holmes whispers the room instructions: no sound, no light, do not sleep, pistol ready.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: Holmes's words come so softly that you must almost read them from the air itself. Each instruction is simple, and each carries life in it.
emotional_choices.choice_question: How do you answer his authority in that moment?

options.label: A
options.text: You answer with a silent nod and set yourself to obey him exactly.
options.outcome: No speech is needed. The nod is enough, and in such work perhaps better than speech, for it spends nothing and promises much. Holmes's arrangements, the chair, the bed, the table corner, the cane, the matches, all fall into a sharper order once you have accepted them without vanity. Obedience here is not submission of judgment, but the practical trust by which men survive a dangerous procedure together. Your own fear, whatever its degree, is therefore converted into rule, posture, and readiness, which is as honourable a use as can be made of it.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes plain, disciplined, and procedural.
options.world_noticed_signal: Holmes does not repeat himself. The absence of repetition is itself a mark of confidence.

options.label: B
options.text: You nod, but keep one questioning glance upon the ventilator before you settle.
options.outcome: The obedience is real, yet not unthinking. Even as you accept his rules, your eye returns to the small opening in the wall which has drawn so much of his dark attention. Holmes notices the glance and allows it, for curiosity grounded in an object is kin to service, not rebellion. Thus your trust takes a slightly different form. You submit to the method, but you also begin to inhabit the problem, and the room acquires for you the quality not only of peril, but of pending explanation.
options.tonal_effect: Narration shades toward forensic curiosity without losing tension.
options.world_noticed_signal: The ventilator, small and ugly in the wall, seems to gather significance merely by being looked at.

options.label: C
options.text: You whisper that he may rely upon you, and touch the revolver as if to seal it.
options.outcome: The words are a risk, but a tiny one, and they come not from vanity but from the old compact between you. Holmes turns his head the least fraction, acknowledging both the pledge and the danger of uttering it. Your fingers rest for an instant on the butt of the revolver, and the gesture gives the promise a bodily weight. There is comfort in such reassurance, though it is bought at the price of one more sound in a room where sound is death. Afterward you are the more careful for having spent that liberty.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes warmer and more companionable for a moment, then tightens again.
options.world_noticed_signal: The whisper dies at once into the shuttered room. Nothing answers it, and yet the silence afterward feels stricter.

emotional_choices.source_moment: The dreadful vigil in absolute darkness, with clock quarters and the cheetah's whine at the window.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: Time has ceased to move in any human fashion and now advances only by the parish clock. Once the long catlike whine sounds at the very window.
emotional_choices.choice_question: What do you do with your fear in the darkness?

options.label: A
options.text: You count the quarters and hold your mind to sequence, refusing the dark any larger dominion.
options.outcome: The method is humble, but it serves. Each quarter struck in the distance becomes a mark upon which the mind may rest instead of wandering among shapeless conjectures. Twelve, one, two, three, the hours do not comfort you, but they divide the dreadful vigil into measurable portions, and measurement is always a kind of resistance. Even the cheetah's whine, shocking as it is at such nearness, is forced into its place among observed facts. Thus fear is not denied, only harnessed to order.
options.tonal_effect: Narration grows measured and classificatory.
options.world_noticed_signal: The clock becomes, for a time, the only civilised voice left in the night.

options.label: B
options.text: You keep your body still and let the fear pass through muscle and breath without yielding it a sound.
options.outcome: There are moments in which courage consists of nothing more brilliant than remaining exactly where one is. You feel the strain in the hands, the throat, the back held rigid against the chair, yet you permit none of it to escape into movement. The cheetah may be at the window, sleep may tug, the dark may press close as a physical thing, but decorum itself becomes an ally. By refusing outward sign, you preserve the plan, and in preserving the plan you preserve the woman for whom it was laid.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes stern, restrained, and bodily precise.
options.world_noticed_signal: NO SIGNAL — state change is minor

options.label: C
options.text: You admit to yourself, briefly and plainly, that this is terror, and then listen harder.
options.outcome: The confession is inward and momentary, but it has value. To name terror when terror is present is not to bow before it, and the honesty of the act clears away the lesser nuisance of pretence. Having granted the fact, you return at once to the business of hearing, the bird outside, the scrape of branch on wall, the long animal cry, and beyond all these the possibility of the one sound for which you wait. The fear remains, but stripped of vagueness it becomes keener and, in a singular way, more useful.
options.tonal_effect: Narration briefly admits direct fear before sharpening into sensory attention.
options.world_noticed_signal: The darkness does not lessen because it is named. It only becomes more exact.

emotional_choices.all_paths_arrive_at: The vigil continues until the first gleam at the ventilator.

emotional_choices.source_moment: The ventilator gleam, smell of burning oil and heated metal, and movement next door.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: A light shows for an instant up toward the ventilator and is gone. Then comes the strong smell of burning oil and heated metal.
emotional_choices.choice_question: How does your mind meet the first sign that the trap is waking?

options.label: A
options.text: You fix upon the smell and gleam as evidence first, forcing yourself to mark them rather than recoil from them.
options.outcome: The effect is immediate. What might have remained a mere increase of dread becomes instead a pair of linked facts, light where no light should be seen, smell that can only mean a lamp newly used in the next room. From those particulars your thought advances, not to a solution yet, but to certainty that the danger is active, humanly managed, and close at hand. The room grows more terrible precisely because it grows more intelligible. You sit the straighter for it.
options.tonal_effect: Narration turns sharply forensic and clue-led.
options.world_noticed_signal: The smell of oil ceases to be atmosphere and becomes testimony.

options.label: B
options.text: You feel the wrongness of it before you understand it, and your hand goes instinctively toward the pistol.
options.outcome: The body answers before the reasoning mind can overtake it. The hand finds the revolver, not from panic, but from an instinct as old as danger itself, and the faint movement seems to gather the whole room into readiness. The gleam and smell remain unexplained, yet they are no longer abstract. They are the heralds of something coming. Such instinct may outrun proof, but it does not outrun peril, and in that shuttered chamber the two are close enough cousins. You are prepared, if not enlightened.
options.tonal_effect: Narration shortens and grows more immediate at the edge of action.
options.world_noticed_signal: Metal answers flesh in the dark as your fingers find the pistol's butt.

options.label: C
options.text: You master the first revulsion and wait for Holmes's movement before altering your own.
options.outcome: The smell is vile in its suggestion, and the little vanished gleam worse, yet you restrain the impulse to shift, start, or whisper. Holmes is the finer instrument in this matter, and so you choose to become the steadier one. If he moves, you will answer; until then, stillness is your contribution to the proof. There is discipline in such waiting, and perhaps a heavier kind of courage than in sudden gesture, for it asks you to remain available to danger without relieving yourself by action.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes cool, tense, and subordinate to Holmes's method.
options.world_noticed_signal: NO SIGNAL — state change is minor

emotional_choices.all_paths_arrive_at: The hiss is heard and Holmes springs to strike.

emotional_choices.source_moment: Roylott's chamber tableau and the moving speckled band.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: The lantern beam lies upon the open safe, the seated body, and the yellow band about the brow. Then the band itself begins to move.
emotional_choices.choice_question: What is your first inward answer to the reveal?

options.label: A
options.text: You force yourself to inventory the room even as horror rises, object by object.
options.outcome: The discipline is severe, but it saves the mind from being wholly mastered by the spectacle. Safe ajar, lantern half-shuttered, dog-whip across the lap, red slippers below, rigid upward stare, yellow band with brown speckles, then the head rearing from the hair. By giving each detail its place, you prevent the whole from dissolving into mere nightmare. The horror does not lessen; indeed, it may sharpen. But it becomes the horror of a true arrangement seen clearly, which is the only kind a witness may finally trust.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes exact, itemised, and controlled under shock.
options.world_noticed_signal: The room yields itself in parts before it overwhelms as a whole.

options.label: B
options.text: You feel first for the dead man's dreadful irony, that his own contrivance has fastened upon him.
options.outcome: Even before the full biological fact is named, the moral shape of the scene strikes you. Here sits the violent man in his own chair, under his own lantern, beside his own safe, with the instrument of his cruelty returned upon his person like judgment made visible. The perception is not sentimental, nor does it excuse the ugliness of the sight; it merely arranges it at once beneath a stern law of consequence. In that instant the chamber becomes not only a crime-scene, but a verdict.
options.tonal_effect: Narration acquires compact moral emphasis.
options.world_noticed_signal: Roylott's rigid stare seems directed not at the ceiling, but at the end of his own design.

options.label: C
options.text: You recoil a step before mastering yourself, the living motion proving worse than the corpse.
options.outcome: The movement is involuntary and entirely human. A dead man may be borne, but death that stirs in his hair is another matter, and the body's first wisdom is distance. Yet you recover at once, for the recoil itself teaches the truth more brutally than any explanation could have done. The band is no fabric, no gipsy hint, no dying fancy, but a living loathsome thing, and the whole mystery contracts in a flash from speculation to fangs. Your horror, though abrupt, is honest witness.
options.tonal_effect: Narration briefly breaks into shock before regaining control.
options.world_noticed_signal: The single backward step is over almost before it is taken, but the room has changed forever by it.

emotional_choices.all_paths_arrive_at: Holmes identifies the swamp adder and secures it in the safe.

posture_shifts.placement: early Setup, as Holmes rises at the signal and catches your sleeve
posture_shifts.narrator_line: Holmes is already moving, and the night seems to ask what sort of companion rises with him.

options.label: A
options.text: I am with you at once.
options.narration_adjustment: You are on your feet almost with the words. Holmes neither turns nor questions you, which in him is a form of confidence.

options.label: B
options.text: One glance first, then we go.
options.narration_adjustment: Your eye goes once more to the middle window before your body follows. The pause is brief, but it gives your resolve the cast of judgment rather than impulse.

options.label: C
options.text: Let me feel the pistol first.
options.narration_adjustment: Your hand goes by instinct to the familiar butt before you move. The gesture is small, professional, and not lost upon Holmes.

posture_shifts.placement: late Setup, crossing the grounds after the breach in the wall
posture_shifts.narrator_line: The grass is damp, the trees close, and each footfall asks whether you mean to be lighter than your fear.

options.label: A
options.text: Heel to toe, and no wasted motion.
options.narration_adjustment: You place each step as if it had first been rehearsed in the mind. The grounds answer with silence, which is all the encouragement such work receives.

options.label: B
options.text: I keep close upon Holmes's shoulder.
options.narration_adjustment: You use Holmes's body as both guide and measure in the dark. It is not weakness, but the practical instinct of men who have gone into danger together before.

options.label: C
options.text: I watch the bushes more than the house.
options.narration_adjustment: The manor remains your goal, but the grounds themselves become your immediate problem. Every laurel mass threatens movement until proved still.

posture_shifts.placement: during Breath beat, just after the baboon darts across the lawn
posture_shifts.narrator_line: The shape has gone, but the body remembers it a moment longer than the mind does.

options.label: A
options.text: Steady now. It is past.
options.narration_adjustment: You master the startle before it can become a second error. The recovery is not elegant, but it is timely, which matters more.

options.label: B
options.text: Good God, what a household.
options.narration_adjustment: The whisper escapes you with more breath than sound. Holmes's answer meets it in kind, and the absurdity briefly takes the edge from terror.

options.label: C
options.text: I say nothing and move again.
options.narration_adjustment: You deny the fright even the dignity of comment. By the time the lawn opens again, it has already been filed away as one more danger among several.

posture_shifts.placement: mid Escalation, under Holmes's whispered rules in the bedroom
posture_shifts.narrator_line: His instructions come one by one, and your face, in the dimness before the lamp is lowered, tells him what kind of obedience he may expect.

options.label: A
options.text: A nod is enough.
options.narration_adjustment: You answer him with the economy his method prefers. Nothing in your manner asks for repetition or comfort.

options.label: B
options.text: I look once to the ventilator.
options.narration_adjustment: Even while you assent, your attention fastens upon the room's smallest impropriety. Holmes notices, and does not discourage it.

options.label: C
options.text: He may rely on me.
options.narration_adjustment: The whisper is slight, but it carries old service in it. Afterward you are the more careful, having spent sound upon assurance.

posture_shifts.placement: mid Escalation, as cane, matches, candle, shutters, and chair settle into place
posture_shifts.narrator_line: Before the lamp goes down, the room offers one last inventory to any eye sharp enough to use it.

options.label: A
options.text: The rope, the bed, the hole.
options.narration_adjustment: Your attention leaps at once to the unnatural alignment of objects. Even in haste, the room begins to look contrived rather than merely old-fashioned.

options.label: B
options.text: The pistol and the chair first.
options.narration_adjustment: You see the room chiefly in terms of where a man may sit, rise, and fire if pressed. It is the physician giving way to the soldier for an hour.

options.label: C
options.text: How little sound all this makes.
options.narration_adjustment: What impresses you most is not the objects, but the noiselessness with which they are handled. Silence itself becomes part of the furniture.

posture_shifts.placement: during Vigil, deep into the absolute darkness
posture_shifts.narrator_line: In absolute darkness a man may either scatter inwardly or draw himself into a smaller, harder shape.

options.label: A
options.text: I count the clock and endure.
options.narration_adjustment: The quarters become your rude companions in the dark. Each one passed is not relief, but proof that you have not yielded.

options.label: B
options.text: I listen for Holmes as much as danger.
options.narration_adjustment: The unseen presence a few feet away steadies you almost as much as it burdens you. Shared peril has its own species of comfort.

options.label: C
options.text: I keep fear in the hands and throat.
options.narration_adjustment: You know exactly where the strain has lodged in the body, and keep it there. So long as it does not pass into sound, it remains governable.

posture_shifts.placement: during Vigil, when the ventilator gleam and oil smell break the long wait
posture_shifts.narrator_line: The darkness is no longer empty now, but occupied by a meaning that has not yet shown its face.

options.label: A
options.text: Lamp next door. Oil and metal.
options.narration_adjustment: You seize the two particulars and bind them together at once. The danger becomes more intelligible, and therefore in one sense more dreadful.

options.label: B
options.text: My hand finds the revolver.
options.narration_adjustment: Thought gives way for an instant to preparation. The pistol's shape in the dark steadies what explanation cannot yet supply.

options.label: C
options.text: I do not move until Holmes does.
options.narration_adjustment: Stillness becomes an active choice rather than a passive one. You hold yourself in reserve, dangerous only when called upon.

posture_shifts.placement: early Twist, at the hiss and Holmes's sudden strike
posture_shifts.narrator_line: The soft sound is scarcely born before Holmes is on his feet and the room bursts, for one instant, into violent light.

options.label: A
options.text: I surge up with the pistol.
options.narration_adjustment: You are moving before the explanation can catch you. The glare blinds, the whistle cuts, and yet your body has already chosen action.

options.label: B
options.text: I try to see what he sees.
options.narration_adjustment: Even in the confusion your eye labours toward the object of Holmes's fury. It is a brave ambition, though the sudden light defeats it.

options.label: C
options.text: I hold and wait for the next sound.
options.narration_adjustment: The room has become too swift for certainty, and you answer uncertainty with stillness. Then the cry comes, making stillness terrible.

posture_shifts.placement: late Twist into Resolution, on the threshold and first sight of Roylott's chamber
posture_shifts.narrator_line: The opened door gives you not merely a room, but an arrangement of facts so grotesque that the eye must choose how to meet it.

options.label: A
options.text: I take in the safe first.
options.narration_adjustment: Your eye goes to the iron box before the man, as if some part of you already suspects that containers may be more eloquent than corpses. The suspicion is soon justified.

options.label: B
options.text: I look to Roylott's hands and lap.
options.narration_adjustment: You search the dead man for the last sign of agency, weapon, or control. The dog-whip lying there answers more than the hands do.

options.label: C
options.text: I halt at the moving band.
options.narration_adjustment: All inventory collapses into one intolerable motion. The room is at once simplified and made more frightful by that concentration.

session_close_design.resolution_prose: The immediate danger is at an end. You stand in that singular chamber with the lamp-light falling in a hard beam upon the iron safe, the saucer of milk, the chair beneath the ventilator, and the dummy bell-rope which hangs there now in its true character, no longer an innocent furnishing but the bridge of a subtle and horrible crime. Holmes, grave and composed after his hardest labours, sets the chain before you point by point: the bed clamped fast, the ventilator which does not ventilate, the whistle in the night, the untraceable poison, the lash looped for handling, the snake driven back in anger upon the man who had schooled it to murder. Helen Stoner is safe; Roylott’s design has failed upon himself; and what was but a dreadful suspicion in the darkness stands now as a body of true facts. There are cases in which the end of fear is less a triumph than a clearing of the air; yet you feel, as the smell of oil still lingers in the room, that this night’s work has been cleanly brought to its issue.
session_close_design.hook_transition: For one moment, at least, the matter rests in the cold light of reason, and that is a relief not lightly valued. Yet the same objects which have yielded up the method now seem to ask another question: by what account shall such facts pass from this room into the world beyond it?

session_end_choice.choice_question: Now that the method is known and Helen is safe, do you mean this truth for official exposure or for a quieter moral settlement?

option_a.text: You mean to press the matter toward formal account, giving authorities as full a truth as the evidence can bear, whatever scandal follows.
option_a.next_session_opens: Morning finds you with Holmes before authority, the iron safe shut, the true facts harder to prove than to know.

option_b.text: You argue that Helen's safety matters more than public process, and that the dead man's own device has already passed the sternest sentence upon him.
option_b.next_session_opens: Dawn comes quietly, with Helen removed to safety and the truest account already withdrawing from public reach.

option_c.text: You choose a middle course, meaning to give the police enough for a workable verdict while keeping the strangest particulars from becoming Helen's lifelong burden.
option_c.next_session_opens: The next account begins not with a scream, but with a statement carefully pared to what the world can bear.

session_end_choice.final_line: The case is solved; its meaning, and its measure, remain in your hands.

session_close_design.next_bridge_guidance: Finalize should stage Holmes's revised conclusions briskly and concretely, using the room's objects as evidentiary inventory. Land the payoff that Helen is safe and the method is known; then pivot without delay into the approved justice-vs-discretion choice, preserving S2_M10 as the terminal moral-authorship room. scene_card.title: The Signal in the Middle Window
scene_card.treatment: Cold-open threshold. The signal light burns in the middle casement; Holmes is on his feet with his hand on your sleeve. The player, as Watson, chooses the posture in which the night operation begins. Concise but load-bearing: the light means Helen has done her part and the window may stand ready.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Launch the live vigil by forcing Watson to commit to a risk posture the instant the signal appears, establishing stealth-is-life and Helen's immediate peril.
scene_card.player_desire: To act at once and not fail the woman waiting across the dark road.
scene_card.live_pressure: The signal is up; every delay may cost Helen her life, yet a misstep could ruin the plan or spring a trap.
scene_card.opening_image: Across the dark road the middle window burns with a single steady light, and Holmes is already upon his feet, his hand at your sleeve, the chill wind waiting beyond the inn.
player_affordances: Urge an immediate silent approach, trusting the plan
Press Holmes to confirm the light is truly Helen's and not a trap
Propose circling the grounds first to learn whether Roylott or a beast is abroad
Check the revolver and ready yourself
Exchange the cover story with the landlord as you leave
canon_must_keep: The light in the middle window is Helen's prearranged signal
You are waiting at the Crown Inn opposite Stoke Moran to act on it tonight
Helen faces the same fate that killed her sister
Stealth is essential; discovery by Roylott would ruin the plan and increase danger
You are Watson, Holmes's trusted armed companion expected to follow into danger
allowed_variance: Watson's degree of hesitation, urgency, or caution
Whether the revolver is mentioned drawn or merely readied
How the cover story to the landlord is phrased
forbidden_expansions: No supernatural reading of the light
Do not resolve the attack method here
Do not let Watson refuse the operation or abandon Holmes
Do not reveal the snake, ventilator theory, or Roylott's plan yet
source_extracts: "That is our signal," said Holmes, springing to his feet; "it comes from the middle window."
A moment later we were out on the dark road, a chill wind blowing in our faces, and one yellow light twinkling in front of us through the gloom to guide us on our sombre errand.
scene_card.exit_condition: The central pressure resolves when Watson has committed to a posture and the pair are moving from the inn toward the house, the operation now irreversibly live.
scene_card.next_bridge: The chosen posture carries you out onto the dark road and toward the breaches in the old park wall, where the grounds and their loose beasts wait.

scene_card.title: The Grounds and the Baboon
scene_card.treatment: The dark grounds. Concise per compress guidance, but a real room: breaches in the old park wall, the walk among trees to the lawn, and the sudden hideous distorted-child figure (the baboon) darting across the grass. Holmes's hand closes like a vice on your wrist before he recovers with a low laugh.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Establish the grounds as a threat-laden traversal and pay off the chosen risk posture through the animal scare, setting the noise profile the player carries into the vigil.
scene_card.player_desire: To reach the window unseen and unheard despite the menace loose on the grounds.
scene_card.live_pressure: A creature moves in the dark; any cry or sound could betray you, and the cheetah may be abroad.

scene_card.title: Staging the Trap
scene_card.treatment: Staging the vigil inside the middle bedroom. Shoes slipped off, shutters noiselessly closed, lamp moved and then turned down. Holmes whispers the operational rules: no sound, no light, stay awake, pistol ready. The player arranges the room — revolver on the table corner, cane, matches, candle — for either safer defence or stronger observation.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Let the player configure the vigil space and internalize the fatal rules of silence and darkness, expressing proof-vs-protection through how the room is staged.

scene_card.live_pressure: Holmes warns the least sound would be fatal and any light would be seen through the ventilator; the trap must be set in near-total silence.
scene_card.opening_image: Inside the middle bedroom all is as you saw it by day, yet each object has drawn into a more sinister relation; Holmes's whisper is so low you must read it from his lips, the cane laid on the bed, the matches and candle at his hand.

scene_card.title: The Dreadful Vigil
scene_card.treatment: The dreadful vigil. Absolute darkness, no sound, not even a breath. The player inhabits felt time: the parish clock booming every quarter, twelve through three, the occasional night-bird, and once at the very window the long catlike whine of the cheetah at liberty. Nothing happens, and that is the point.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Stretch felt time so silence and uncertainty are truly experienced before the violent reversal, making the climax land.
scene_card.player_desire: To endure the wait, stay awake and alert, and not break the silence.
scene_card.live_pressure: Endless darkness and strain; the cheetah is loose outside, and the attack could come at any unknown moment.

scene_card.next_bridge: The long stillness breaks: a momentary gleam shows up toward the ventilator, and a smell begins to gather in the dark.

scene_card.title: The Gleam at the Ventilator
scene_card.treatment: The first wrongness. A momentary gleam of light shows in the direction of the ventilator, then vanishes, succeeded by a strong smell of burning oil and heated metal — someone next door has lit a dark-lantern. A gentle sound of movement, then silence, and the smell grows stronger through the strained half-hour.

scene_card.title: The Strike and the Cry
scene_card.treatment: The reversal. A very gentle soothing sound, like a small jet of steam from a kettle. Holmes springs from the bed, strikes a match, and lashes furiously at the bell-pull, yelling 'You see it, Watson?' The sudden glare blinds Watson; a low clear whistle sounds; Holmes's face is deadly pale with horror and loathing. Then the most horrible cry breaks from the night and swells and dies.

scene_card.title: Into Roylott's Room

scene_card.title: The Speckled Band
scene_card.treatment: The crime-scene tableau. The dark-lantern's half-open shutter throws a beam on the ajar iron safe. Roylott sits in his grey dressing-gown, bare ankles, red Turkish slippers, the dog-whip across his lap, chin cocked upward, eyes fixed in a rigid stare. Round his brow a peculiar yellow band with brownish speckles — which begins to move, rearing the squat diamond head of a snake. 'The band! the speckled band!'

scene_card.title: The Swamp Adder Contained
scene_card.treatment: Containment and moral verdict. Holmes cries 'It is a swamp adder — the deadliest snake in India,' notes Roylott died within ten seconds, and speaks the maxim that violence recoils upon the violent and the schemer falls into his own pit. He draws the dog-whip from the dead man's lap, nooses the reptile's neck, carries it at arm's length, and thrusts it into the iron safe, closing it.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Resolve the immediate danger through Holmes's decisive containment and deliver the moral shape of the ending while the player acts alongside him.

scene_card.title: The Debrief and the Verdict
scene_card.treatment: The debrief and final synthesis. Holmes lays out the rational retrospective chain as interactive Q&A: his erroneous first conclusion from insufficient data (the gipsies, the word 'band'), his reconsideration when danger could come from neither window nor door, the ventilator and dummy bell-rope, the clamped bed as a bridge for something passing through, the snake, the untraceable Eastern poison, the whistle to recall it, the milk to train it. Then the evidence (chair-standing, safe, saucer of milk, whipcord, the metallic clang of the safe door) and his admission that he lit the light and attacked, driving the snake back to turn upon its master. Compressed per guidance into one closing room, ending on the authored justice-vs-discretion choice.
scene_card.runtime_goal: Assemble the complete rational solution and moral coda through player-driven questioning, confirm the recoil causality, and close the session on how the truth should live afterward.
scene_card.player_desire: To understand exactly how the murder worked and how Holmes turned it back on Roylott.
scene_card.live_pressure: The night is won, but the full truth is still unspoken; Watson (and the player) must piece together how it was done and decide how it should be carried into the world.
scene_card.opening_image: The lamp-light falls hard upon the iron safe, the saucer of milk, the chair beneath the ventilator, and the dummy bell-rope in its true character; Holmes, grave and composed after his hardest labours, sets the chain before you point by point.

scene_card.exit_condition: The pressure resolves when the full clue-to-inference chain and the recoil causality are understood, and the player has chosen the moral authorship of the case record — the final cash-out of the session.
scene_card.next_bridge: For one moment, at least, the matter rests in the cold light of reason, and that is a relief not lightly valued. Yet the same objects which have yielded up the method now seem to ask another question: by what account shall such facts pass from this room into the world beyond it?

event_roles.why: The signal appearing and the departure into the night is the Entry Point and the first live threshold: Watson commits to the operation's risk posture (stealth/haste/vigilance) at the instant Helen's survival goes from theoretical to immediate. A load-bearing identity/commitment pressure.

The grounds crossing with the distorted-child (baboon) scare is a genuinely inhabitable room: movement under threat, noise discipline, ambient animal menace, and Holmes's vice-grip startle reveal relationship under strain. Guidance marks it must_compress, so it is concise but still playable.

Staging the vigil — shoes off, shutters closed, revolver, cane, matches, candle placed, lamp extinguished — is a rich procedural room where the player configures the trap and chooses proof-vs-protection. Must-breathe.

The dreadful vigil in absolute darkness is the emotional core of felt time: sensory deprivation, the clock striking, the cheetah's whine. This must breathe as its own inhabited room where nothing happens yet everything is at stake.

The gleam at the ventilator and the growing smell of burning oil and heated metal is one strong sensory image that breaks the darkness — a short, sharp playable beat of dawning wrongness. Must-breathe, given its own moment.

The soft steam-jet hiss, Holmes springing up, the match, the furious lashing at the bell-pull, and the horrible shriek is the violent reversal — the session's central pressure resolving in a room the player inhabits under maximum tension. Choice of decisive action vs patient observation lives here.

The decision to take the pistol and enter Roylott's room is a short duty-vs-self-preservation crossing into the aftermath. Guidance marks it must_compress, so it is a brief threshold beat rather than a full room.

The crime-scene tableau — Roylott dead, dressing-gown, dog-whip, open safe, and the speckled band that rears into a living snake — is the singular reveal. Must-breathe as an examinable horror room where the mystery's solution becomes visible.
Holmes naming the swamp adder, speaking the moral aphorism, and noosing the snake into the iron safe is the decisive containment — a room of resolution and forensic action. Must-breathe.

Holmes's revised conclusions (insufficient data, ventilator, dummy rope, clamped bed, snake bridge) are the required rational retrospective synthesis. Folded with 122 into a single debrief room; must_compress so delivered as interactive Q&A rather than a monologue dump.

The evidence account (chair-standing, safe, saucer of milk, whipcord, metallic clang) and Holmes confirming he lit the light and attacked, driving the snake back to turn upon Roylott, completes the moral shape. Compressed into the same debrief; recoil causality is the load-bearing canon.
